Title: Preliminary development of DNA aptamer-Fc conjugate opsonins
Target: Poly-alpha-D-glutamic acid (α-PDGA-coated magnetic beads (MBs)) part of the B.anthracis capsule
Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers against α-PDGA-MBs and couple them to Fc fragments of murine IgG DNA to act as potential opsonins.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Increase in phagocytic index (P.I.) up to threefold in the first 30 min of exposure to α-PDGA-MBs.

Cytotoxicity (cell viability): Cell viability ranged from 90% to 95% in all experiments.

Objective/Mechanism: Identify an aptamer against the whole cell and induce strong depolarization of the bacterial cell membrane (Inhibition of growth of S. enteritidis and S. typhimurium in bacterial cultures and a decrease in their membrane potential).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: 73 ± 15% inhibition ratio for S. enteritidis and 43 ± 4% (SE-20, 60nt) in S. enteritidis.

Title: Aptamer against mannose-capped lipoarabinomannan inhibits virulent Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection in mice and rhesus monkeys
Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers that bind to and inhibit ManLAM recognition by host cells and ManLAM-induced immunosuppression of CD11c+ dendritic cells (DCs).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: ZXL1 bound to virulent M. tb H37Rv much more strongly (52.2%) than to the other Mycobacteria strains tested, M. smegmatis (2.5%) and BCG (13.9%). LPS-stimulated human DC groups showed that ZXL1 decreased IL-10 production by 31–36% and increased IL-12 production by 52–91%, thereby reducing the progression of infection and bacterial loads in mice and rhesus monkeys.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): ZXL1 showed no significant cytotoxicity at concentrations ranging from 2 to 15 microM at the 168-hour test.

Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Displayed linear responses in the range of 0.1 nM to 10 nM EcOMPs and LOD of 10 nM in less than 1 h.

Title: A simple aptamer biosensor for Salmonellae enteritidis based on fluorescence-switch signaling graphene oxide
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a fluorescent aptasensor with an aptamer functionalized into graphene oxide to detect S. enteritidis.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Can detect as low as 40 CFU/mL of S. enteritidis in 30 min.

Title: Neutralization of staphylococcal enterotoxin B by an aptamer antagonist
Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers that bind to and block SEB-mediated toxic shock (TSS) in vitro.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Inhibited SEB-mediated PBMC proliferation of 93% and TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-2, and IFN-γ in culture supernatants were reduced by 77, 97, 64, 96, and 99%, respectively. 90% survival of mouse models of SEB-induced TSS.
Modification: 5′-Polyethylene glycol (PEG) with 5'-Amidation (NH₂) and 3’-Inverted Thymidine (3'-idT) and 5'-Biotinylated or 5'-FITC Labeled
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): Showed no cytotoxic effects on PBMCs.

Title: Antibiotic loaded nanocapsules functionalized with aptamer gates for targeted destruction of pathogen
Objective/Mechanism: Aptamer-gated nanocapsules for the specific targeting of vancomycin to bacteria for the controlled release of vancomycin.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: 15-fold increase of efficacy for vancomycin with MIC of 0.420 μg/mL.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): MICs of vancomycin-nanoparticles for S. epidermidis (control) were found to be 6.295 µg/mL.

Outcome/Inhibitory effect: A calibration curve is obtained in the range of 15 to 1.5 × 10(6) CFU/mL with a limit of detection of 15 CFU/mL.

Title: Diazonium-based impedimetric aptasensor for the rapid label-free detection of Salmonella typhimurium in food sample
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a label-free impedimetric aptamer-based biosensor for S. typhimurium detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Rapid (30 min) detection with a concentration range of 1×10(1) to 1×10(8) CFU/mL and limit of detection (LOD) of 6 CFU/mL.

Title: Rapid and Selective Detection of Pathogenic Bacteria in Bloodstream Infections with Aptamer-Based Recognition
Objective/Mechanism: Aptamer-based capture platform using Fe3O4@mTiO2 magnetic nanoparticles for the detection of bacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a favourable bacterial-capture efficiency of about 80% even at low infectious doses (10–2000 CFU/mL).

Title: Rapid and Selective Detection of Pathogenic Bacteria in Bloodstream Infections with Aptamer-Based Recognition
Objective/Mechanism: Aptamer-based capture platform using Fe3O4@mTiO2 magnetic nanoparticles for the detection of bacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a favourable bacterial-capture efficiency of about 80% even at low infectious doses (10–2000 CFU/mL).

Title: Highly sensitive detection of lipopolysaccharides using an aptasensor based on hybridization chain reaction
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptasensor assay based on hybridization chain reaction (HCR) to detect LPS.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a relatively low detection limit (1.73 ng/mL) with a linear response range of 1–10(5) ng/mL.

Title: Dual Recognition Strategy for Specific and Sensitive Detection of Bacteria Using Aptamer-Coated Magnetic Beads and Antibiotic-Capped Gold Nanoclusters
Objective/Mechanism: Aptamer-coated magnetic beads (Apt-MB) and Van-functionalized fluorescent gold nanoclusters (AuNCs@Van) were employed for specific capture of SA.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Sensitive quantification of SA in the range of 32–10(8) cfu/mL with the detection limit of 16 cfu/mL via fluorescence intensity.

Title: Duplex Identification of Staphylococcus aureus by Aptamer and Gold Nanoparticles
Objective/Mechanism: Develop an aptamer-AuNPs-based colorimetric method for duplex identification of S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: AuNPs as a sensor could well distinguish S. aureus from S. enteritidis and P. mirabilis.

Title: DNA aptamers for the detection of Haemophilus influenzae type b by cell SELEX
Objective/Mechanism: Identify an aptamer against Hib for the detection of H. influenzae.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Clone 63 could detect Hib in patients’ CSF samples at 60 CFU/mL.

Title: DNA aptamers for the detection of Haemophilus influenzae type b by cell SELEX
Objective/Mechanism: Identify an aptamer against Hib for the detection of H. influenzae.

Title: Magnetic Nanoparticles-based Aptasensor Using Gold Nanoparticles as Colorimetric Probes for the Detection of Salmonella typhimurium
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a colorimetric aptasensor for S. typhimurium detection using gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) and magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The assay shows a linear response over a range of 25 to 10(5) cfu/mL, and the detection limit was improved to 10 cfu/mL.

Title: Dual-excitation upconverting nanoparticle and quantum dot aptasensor for multiplexed food pathogen detection
Objective/Mechanism: Dual-excitation aptasensing platform based on the luminescent nanoparticles (QDs and UCNPs) for the detection of Salmonella typhimurium and Staphylococcus aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Linear detection range: 50 to 10⁶ cfu/mL; LOD: 16 cfu/mL (S. aureus).

Title: Dual-excitation upconverting nanoparticle and quantum dot aptasensor for multiplexed food pathogen detection
Objective/Mechanism: Dual-excitation aptasensing platform based on the luminescent nanoparticles (QDs and UCNPs) for the detection of Salmonella typhimurium and Staphylococcus aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Linear detection range: 50 to 10⁶ cfu/mL; LOD: 28 cfu/mL (S. typhimurium).

Title: A paper based graphene-nanocauliflower hybrid composite for point of care biosensing
Objective/Mechanism: Develop electrochemical biosensing platform using graphene paper functionalized with fractal platinum nanocauliflower for detection of E. coli O157:H7.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Detection limit (LOD) of ~4 CFU/mL with linear range of 4 to 10(5) CFU/mL and a response time of 12 min.

Title: Quantitative Label-Free Listeria Analysis Based On Aptamer Modified Nanoporous Sensor
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a nanoporous sensor with aptamer combined porous anodic aluminium oxide membrane for detection of L. monocytogenes.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved detection within 10 min, with a high sensitivity of 100 CFU/mL and a good linear range between 100 and 1250 CFU/mL.

Title: Vibrio parahaemolyticus detection aptasensor using surface-enhanced Raman scattering
Objective/Mechanism: A SERS-based aptasensor was developed using Au@Ag core-shell nanoparticles for the detection of V. parahaemolyticus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a concentration in the linear range of 10–10(6) cfu/mL, with a limit of detection of 10 cfu/mL.

Title: SERS aptasensor detection of Salmonella typhimurium using a magnetic gold nanoparticle and gold nanoparticle based sandwich structure
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a SERS aptasensor using aptamer-functionalized magnetic gold nanoparticles (MGNPs) and mercaptobenzoic acid (4-MBA) functionalized gold nanoparticles (GNPs) based sandwich structure for the detection of S. typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibit a good linear range from 10 cfu/mL to 10(7) cfu/mL, and the LOD is 5 cfu/mL.

Title: Development of an aptamer-ampicillin conjugate for treating biofilms
Objective/Mechanism: Aptamer-ampicillin conjugate (Apt3-Amp) to inhibit biofilm formation.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Biofilms containing the conjugate had the lowest survival ratio (37.22 ± 1.12%) compared with control conjugates.

Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a LOD of 10(3) CFU/mL for S. Enteritidis.

Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers that bind to and develop a graphene oxide-based fluorometric assay to detect FbpA.

Title: A single-stranded DNA aptamer against mannose-capped lipoarabinomannan enhances anti-tuberculosis activity of macrophages through downregulation of lipid-sensing nuclear receptor peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ expression
Objective/Mechanism: Downregulate PPARγ expression by blocking the binding of ManLAM to MR on macrophages, and ZXL1 enhances IL-1β and IL-12 mRNA expression and cytokine production in ManLAM-treated macrophages but decreases IL-10 production.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The percentage of macrophages that took up iH37Rv decreased from 15.9% to 7.2%, thereby inhibiting ManLAM-induced immunosuppression of DCs.

Title: DNA aptamer functionalized gold nanostructures for molecular recognition and photothermal inactivation of methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus
Objective/Mechanism: Aptamer-functionalized gold nanorods (Apt@Au NRs) for inactivation of MRSA with targeted photothermal therapy (PTT).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Over 95% inactivation of MRSA cells within 2 min.

Cytotoxicity (cell viability): Aptamers had no intrinsic bacteriostatic and/or bactericidal activity.

Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The detection time for M. tuberculosis was 70 min, and the detection limit was 100 cfu/mL.

Title: Evaluation of Staphylococcus aureus DNA aptamer by enzyme-linked aptamer assay and isothermal titration calorimetry
Objective/Mechanism: ELAA and ITC to study impact of temperature and ion concentration in the binding of aptamer to its target on surface of bacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Both temperature and salt concentration directly influenced the 3D structure of the DNA molecule under specified experimental conditions, thereby altering the aptamer's affinity for its target.

Title: Selection, characterization, and application of DNA aptamers for detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis secreted protein MPT64
Objective/Mechanism: Identify DNA aptamers against MPT64 protein.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The ELONA assay had a sensitivity and specificity of 91.3% and 90% on sputum samples.

Title: Upconversion nanoparticles based FRET aptasensor for rapid and ultrasenstive bacteria detection
Objective/Mechanism: Upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) based FRET aptasensor (UCNPs-cDNA from AuNPs-aptamers) for detecting E. coli in tap/pond water and milk.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a detection range of 5–10(6) cfu/mL and a detection limit of 3 cfu/mL in 20 min.

Objective/Mechanism: Identify modified aptamers that were isolated against Escherichia coli DH5α cells.

Title: Electrochemical determination of M. tuberculosis antigen based on Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) and functionalized carbon nanotubes hybrid platform
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an electrochemical aptasensor based on MWCNT-doped PEDOT nano-composite for the detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibits a LOD of 0.5 fg/mL within 15 min for the detection of M. tb antigenic protein with recovery in between (88–95)%.
Stability: The stability of the aptasensor is 27 days at 4°C, and the reusability is 7 times after repeated regeneration with 50 mM NaOH.

Title: Fullerene-doped polyaniline as new redox nanoprobe and catalyst in electrochemical aptasensor for ultrasensitive detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis MPT64 antigen in human serum
Objective/Mechanism: Electrochemical aptasensor based on GNPs-C60-PAn labelled with signal aptamer for the determination of MTB antigen.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: A wide linear detection range of 0.02 to 1000 pg/mL was obtained, with a detection limit of 20 fg/mL for MPT64.

Title: Fullerene-doped polyaniline as new redox nanoprobe and catalyst in electrochemical aptasensor for ultrasensitive detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis MPT64 antigen in human serum
Objective/Mechanism: Electrochemical aptasensor based on GNPs-C60-PAn labelled with signal aptamer for the determination of MTB antigen.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: A wide linear detection range of 0.02 to 1000 pg/mL was obtained, with a detection limit of 20 fg/mL for MPT64.

Title: A magnetic relaxation switch aptasensor for the rapid detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa using superparamagnetic nanoparticles
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a magnetic relaxation switch (MRSw) aptasensor (SPIO-aptamer) for the determination of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in real food and drinking water samples.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibit a linear range from 10(0) cfu/mL to 10(6) cfu/mL, and a detection limit of 50 cfu/mL was obtained within 40 mins.

Title: Novel impedimetric aptasensor for label-free detection of Escherichia coli O157:H7
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a novel impedance-based aptasensor for the detection of E. coli O157:H7.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a broad range from 10(1) to 10(5) cfu/mL with the LOD about 2.9 × 10(2) cfu/mL with a detection time of 30 min.

Title: SERS aptasensor for Salmonella typhimurium detection based on spiny gold nanoparticles
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a novel SGNPs-based SERS aptasensor functionalized with p-MBA for the detection of S. typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display linear range 10(1) cfu/mL to 10(5) cfu/mL, with a limit of detection (LOD) of 4 cfu/mL.

Title: Development of An Impedimetric Aptasensor for the Detection of Staphylococcus aureus
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an impedimetric aptasensor for the detection of S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Showed a limit of detection of 10 CFU/mL within 10 minutes.

Title: Antimicrobial peptide-loaded gold nanoparticle-DNA aptamer conjugates as highly effective antibacterial therapeutics against Vibrio vulnificus
Objective/Mechanism: The AuNP-AptHis conjugate delivers the HPA3P(His) peptide into host cells, inducing bacterial cell death by disrupting membrane integrity.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Compared with that of buffer- or AuNP-AptHis-incubated cells, the number of viable V. vulnificus cells in the AuNP-AptHis-HPA3PHis-treated cells decreased by 90% in 10 min. All infected mice injected with AuNP-AptHis-HPA3PHis survived until 120 h.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): HPA3PHis and AuNP-Apt(His)-HPA3P(His) did not exhibit cytotoxicity against HeLa cells and mouse erythrocytes up to 10 µM.

Title: An Electrochemical Aptasensor Using Coaxial Capillary with Magnetic Nanoparticle, Urease Catalysis and PCB Electrode for Rapid and Sensitive Detection of Escherichia coli O157:H7
Objective/Mechanism: Develop an electrochemical aptasensor for rapid and sensitive detection of E. coli O157:H7 that relies on aptamer and urease-modified GNPs.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Able to detect E. coli as low as 10(1) CFU/mL in 3 h, and the mean recovery of E. coli in the spiked pasteurized milk was ~99%.

Title: Intuitive Label-Free SERS Detection of Bacteria Using Aptamer-Based in Situ Silver Nanoparticles Synthesis
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a SERS-based aptasensor using aptamer@AgNPs for the detection of bacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a linear concentration, ranging from 10(1) to 10(7) cfu/mL with the detection limit of 1.5 cfu/mL.

Title: Intuitive Label-Free SERS Detection of Bacteria Using Aptamer-Based in Situ Silver Nanoparticles Synthesis
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a SERS-based aptasensor using aptamer@AgNPs for the detection of bacteria.

Title: A novel aptasensor for the colorimetric detection of S. typhimurium based on gold nanoparticles
Objective/Mechanism: Colorimetric aptasensor was developed based on color changing GNPs for the detection of S. typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Quantitative detection of S. typhimurium from 10(2) to 10(7) cfu/mL with a detection limit as low as 56 cfu/mL.

Title: A chemiluminescent aptasensor based on rolling circle amplification and Co2+/N-(aminobutyl)-N-(ethylisoluminol) functional flowerlike gold nanoparticles for Salmonella typhimurium detection
Objective/Mechanism: Chemiluminescent aptasensor based on rolling circle amplification (RCA) using Co2+/ABEI-AuNFs-cDNA complex was developed for the detection of S. typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The limit of detection (LOD) was 10 cfu/mL. The method exhibited excellent selectivity over non-target bacteria.

Title: Graphene-based label-free electrochemical aptasensor for rapid and sensitive detection of foodborne pathogen
Objective/Mechanism: rGO-azophloxine (AP) nanocomposite aptasensor was developed for the detection of foodborne pathogens.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a linear range of detection from 10(8) to 10(1) cfu/mL with a detection limit of 10(1) cfu/mL.
Stability: Aptasensor showed good stability for up to 20 days, with a 5.1% increase in current response when stored in ultrapure water at 4°C.

Title: An aptamer-based PCR method coupled with magnetic immunoseparation for sensitive detection of Salmonella Typhimurium in ground turkey
Objective/Mechanism: Aptamer-based PCR method coupled with magnetic immunoseparation was developed to detect S. Typhimurium from ground turkey.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Able to detect 10(2) CFU/mL of S. Typhimurium in pure culture, and 10(3) CFU/mL of S. Typhimurium in ground turkey.

Title: Fluorometric graphene oxide-based detection of Salmonella enteritis using a truncated DNA aptamer
Objective/Mechanism: Truncated aptamer was used to develop a fluorometric graphene oxide (GO) based assay for the detection of S. enteriditis.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: LOD of 38 and 25 cfu/mL for the full length SE54 and SE54T, respectively, with a linear response from 10(2) to 10(7) cfu/mL.

Title: Fluorometric graphene oxide-based detection of Salmonella enteritis using a truncated DNA aptamer
Objective/Mechanism: Truncated aptamer was used to develop a fluorometric graphene oxide (GO) based assay for the detection of S. enteriditis.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: LOD of 38 and 25 cfu/mL for the full length SE54 and SE54T, respectively with a linear response from 10(2) to 10(7) cfu/mL.

Title: Thioaptamer targeted discoidal microparticles increase self immunity and reduce Mycobacterium tuberculosis burden in mice
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a targeting system using CD44 thioaptamers (TA)-conjugated discoidal silicon mesoporous microparticles (SMP) to enhance accumulation of these agents/carriers in the infected macrophages in the lungs.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: CD44TA-SMP treatment increased IP-10 (CXCL-10), MCP-1, MCP-2, and RANTES, with no change in IL-6 release compared to the control.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): In uninfected murine and human macrophages, SMP and CD44TA-SMP did not affect the cell viability.

Title: Dual-Recognition Förster Resonance Energy Transfer Based Platform for One-Step Sensitive Detection of Pathogenic Bacteria Using Fluorescent Vancomycin-Gold Nanoclusters and Aptamer-Gold Nanoparticles
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a dual-molecular FRET platform based on the recognition of bacterial cell walls by antibiotic and aptamer molecules, respectively, for the detection of pathogenic bacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Shows a linear concentration of Staph. aureus in the range from 20 to 10(8) cfu/mL with a detection limit of 10 cfu/mL.

Title: A point-of-need enzyme linked aptamer assay for Mycobacterium tuberculosis detection using a smartphone
Objective/Mechanism: Smartphone-based method using enzyme-linked aptamers for point-of-need M.tb detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The direct dot-blot system provided a lower limit of quantitation of 10(4) CFU/mL and greater accuracy.

Title: A point-of-need enzyme linked aptamer assay for Mycobacterium tuberculosis detection using a smartphone
Objective/Mechanism: Smartphone-based method using enzyme-linked aptamers for point-of-need M.tb detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The limit of quantitation (LOQ) for indirect assays was 10(5) CFU/mL.

Title: A rapid and visual aptasensor for Lipopolysaccharides detection based on the bulb-like triplex turn-on switch coupled with HCR-HRP nanostructures
Target Organism: Escherichia Coli (E. Coli) O111:B4 and O111:B5
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a turn-on sensor based on a bulb-like triplex turn-on switch (BTTS) for the detection of lipopolysaccharides.

Title: A rapid and visual aptasensor for Lipopolysaccharides detection based on the bulb-like triplex turn-on switch coupled with HCR-HRP nanostructures
Target Organism: Escherichia Coli (E. Coli) O111:B4 and O111:B5
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a turn-on sensor based on a bulb-like triplex turn-on switch (BTTS) for the detection of lipopolysaccharides.

Title: A rapid and visual aptasensor for Lipopolysaccharides detection based on the bulb-like triplex turn-on switch coupled with HCR-HRP nanostructures
Target Organism: Escherichia Coli (E. Coli) O111:B4 and O111:B5
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a turn-on sensor based on a bulb-like triplex turn-on switch (BTTS) for the detection of lipopolysaccharides.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The sensor has a linear calibration range of 1-150 ng/mL and a detection limit of 50 pg/mL, quantitatively, with the portable spectrophotometer, and 20 ng/mL, semi-quantitatively, with the naked eye.

Title: A rapid and visual aptasensor for Lipopolysaccharides detection based on the bulb-like triplex turn-on switch coupled with HCR-HRP nanostructures
Target Organism: Escherichia Coli (E. Coli) O111:B4 and O111:B5
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a turn-on sensor based on a bulb-like triplex turn-on switch (BTTS) for the detection of lipopolysaccharides.

Title: Colorimetric aptasensor for the detection of Salmonella enterica serovar typhimurium using ZnFe2O4-reduced graphene oxide nanostructures as an effective peroxidase mimetics
Objective/Mechanism: The colorimetric aptasensor platform was developed based on ZnFe2O4/rGO nanostructures, which act as an artificial enzyme (mimetic) that catalyses the oxidation of TMB by H2O2 to detect S. typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The limit of detection (LOD) of 11 cfu/mL, and the detection range was 11 to 1.10 × 10(5) cfu/mL of S. typhimurium in buffer solution.

Title: Colorimetric aptasensor for the detection of Salmonella enterica serovar typhimurium using ZnFe2O4-reduced graphene oxide nanostructures as an effective peroxidase mimetics
Objective/Mechanism: The colorimetric aptasensor platform was developed based on ZnFe2O4/rGO nanostructures, which act as an artificial enzyme (mimetic) that catalyses the oxidation of TMB by H2O2 to detect S. typhimurium.

Title: (1→3)-β-D-glucan aptamers labeled with technetium-99m: Biodistribution and imaging in experimental models of bacterial and fungal infection
Objective/Mechanism: Radiolabeled aptamers were evaluated to identify infectious foci caused by bacterial cells.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The target/non-target ratios were 3.17 ± 0.22 for seq6 in S. aureus-infected animals.
Stability: In vitro stability of seq6 aptamer labelled with 99mTc in the presence of 0.9% saline, plasma, and cysteine excess (molar ratio) was above 84.2 ± 2.9% in all cases at 24hrs.

Title: Detection of bacterial infection by a technetium-99m-labeled peptidoglycan aptamer
Objective/Mechanism: Radiolabeled aptamers were evaluated for biodistribution studies and scintigraphic imaging in infection‐bearing mice.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a high target-to-non-target (T/NT) ratio of 4.7 ± 0.9 at 1.5 h and 4.6 ± 0.1 at 3.0 h in bacterial-infected models.
Stability: Radiolabeling yields were superior to 90% and 99mTc‐Antibac1 was highly stable in the presence of saline, plasma, and cysteine up to 6 h.
Half-life: Distribution half-life: 6.7 min and Elimination half-life: 41.3 min.

Title: Development of gold nanoparticle-aptamer-based LSPR sensing chips for the rapid detection of Salmonella typhimurium in pork meat
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a portable LSPR biosensor-based device on gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) for the detection of Salmonella typhimurium in pork meat samples.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Limit of detection (LOD) of 10(4) cfu/mL in both pure culture and spiked pork samples, and total analysis time of 30-35 minutes.

Title: AgBr nanoparticles/3D nitrogen-doped graphene hydrogel for fabricating all-solid-state luminol-electrochemiluminescence Escherichia coli aptasensors
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a ECL aptasensor based on amine-functionalized E. coli aptamer and luminol/AgBr/3DNGH for the detection of E. coli.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Linear response range from 0.5 to 500 cfu/mL and Limit of Detection (LOD) of 0.17 cfu/mL.
Stability: No obvious change was observed for the response of a BSA/aptamer/GA/CHIT/luminol/AgBr/3DNGH/GCE when stored at 4°C for 12 d, indicating an acceptable stability of the aptasensor.

Title: Aptamer biosensor for Salmonella typhimurium detection based on luminescence energy transfer from Mn2+-doped NaYF4:Yb, Tm upconverting nanoparticles to gold nanorods
Objective/Mechanism: A LET method based on UCNPs and gold nanorods (Au NRs) was developed for the determination of Salmonella typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Linear range: 12 to 5×10^5 cfu/mL and Limit of Detection (LOD): 11 cfu/mL.

Title: Aptamer based voltammetric biosensor for the detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigen MPT64
Objective/Mechanism: Develop an aptaelectrode based on graphene modified iron-oxide chitosan hybrid (CHIT-IO-GR) nanocomposite film deposited on fluorine tin oxide (FTO) for the detection of the M. tb. specific antigen MPT64.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.9 fg/mL within 20 min and a linear range from 1.0 × 10(5) fg/mL to 1.0 fg/mL.
Stability: The biosensor retained about 80% of its initial activity after 10 uses and good stability of 17 day.

Title: Copper-Based Metal-Organic Framework Nanoparticles with Peroxidase-Like Activity for Sensitive Colorimetric Detection of Staphylococcus aureus
Objective/Mechanism: A colorimetric method for the detection of S. aureus was developed using aptamer-modified Cu-MOF nanoparticles.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The linear range for S. aureus detection is 50-10,000 CFU/mL, with a detection limit of 20 CFU/mL.

Title: An enhanced chemiluminescence resonance energy transfer aptasensor based on rolling circle amplification and WS2 nanosheet for Staphylococcus aureus detection
Objective/Mechanism: A chemiluminescence resonance energy transfer aptasensor was developed for the detection of S. aureus with Co2+ enhanced N-(aminobutyl)-N-(ethylisoluminol) (ABEI) functional flowerlike gold nanoparticles (Co2+/ABEI-AuNFs) and WS2 nanosheet.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The CL signal was found to be linear within the range of 50 cfu/mL to 1.5 × 10(5) cfu/mL, and the limit of detection was 15 cfu/mL.

Title: Fabricating a Novel Raman Spectroscopy-Based Aptasensor for Rapidly Sensing Salmonella typhimurium
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) based aptasensor with Raman active molecule attached GNRs and cDNA for the detection of Salmonella typhimurium (ST).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Observed linear ST concentration from 56 to 56 × 10(7) cfu/mL with a LOD of 9 cfu/mL.

Title: Graphene Field-Effect Transistors for the Sensitive and Selective Detection of Escherichia coli Using Pyrene-Tagged DNA Aptamer
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a biosensing platform using graphene field-effect transistors (APG-FETs) with the aid of pyrene-tagged DNA aptamers for E. coli detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieve a detection limit of 10(2) CFU/mL for E. coli within 72 s.

Title: Rolling circle amplification based amperometric aptamer/immuno hybrid biosensor for ultrasensitive detection of Vibrio parahaemolyticus
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an antibody-aptamer-based hetero-sandwich amperometric biosensor for the detection of V. parahaemolyticus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a range of 2.2 to 2.2 x10(8) cfu/mL, and the limit of detection is as low as 2 cfu/mL.
Stability: After 2 weeks of storage at 4°C, the fabricated electrochemical aptasensor retains about 95.2% of its initial sensing current response.

Title: Development of an aptasensor using reduced graphene oxide chitosan complex to detect Salmonella
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a rGO-CHI electrochemical aptasensor to detect Salmonella.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Had a wide detection range of 10(1) to 10(6) CFU/mL with a low limit of detection of 10(1) CFU/mL.

Title: A simple dendrimer-aptamer based microfluidic platform for E. coli O157:H7 detection and signal intensification by rolling circle amplification
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a dendrimer-aptamer microfluidic detection system with Rolling circle amplification (RCA) for the detection of E. coli O157:H7 cells.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: RCA was able to enhance detection signals by up to 50 times, and the limit of detection of the system was reduced to 10(2) cells/mL.

Title: Combat biofilm by bacteriostatic aptamer-functionalized graphene oxide

Outcome/Inhibitory effect: 93.3 ± 3.4% inhibition ratio at the initial stage of biofilm formation and 84.6 ± 5.1% degradation ratio on formed biofilms.

Objective/Mechanism: A nitrocellulose membrane-based integrated microfluidic system for detecting bacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a limit of detection as low as 450 CFU/reaction for AB within 40 minutes and a linear range from 4.5×10(4) to 4.5 CFU/reaction.

Title: Selective capture and sensitive fluorometric determination of Pseudomonas aeruginosa by using aptamer modified magnetic nanoparticles
Objective/Mechanism: A fluorometric assay for the detection of the food pathogen P. aeruginosa based on hybridization of aptamer and FAM-cDNA (aptamer&FAM-cDNA@MNPs).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a linear range between 10 and 10(8) cfu/mL, with a detection limit as low as 1 cfu/mL. The detection process can be finished within <1.5 h.

Objective/Mechanism: A localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) based sensing platform was developed to detect the whole-cell Pseudomonas aeruginosa strain PAO1.

Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Shows a wide linear range of 1.28 × 10(3)-2.00 × 10(7) cfu/mL with a detection limit of 100 cfu/mL within 2 h.

Objective/Mechanism: Identify and develop an aptamer-based fluorescence assay (aptamer-CDs/GO system) for culture-independent detection of P. aeruginosa.

Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The Limit of Detection (LOD) achieved was 10 CFU/mL in phosphate-buffered saline and 100 CFU/mL in milk samples with a linear range from 10 to 10(6) CFU/mL.

Title: Use of DNA aptamer for sandwich type detection of Listeria monocytogenes
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a two-site binding sandwich assay for capture and detection of L. monocytogenes.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display LOD of 2.5 CFU L. monocytogenes in 500 μl buffer and 10 CFU/25 g turkey deli meat sample.

Objective/Mechanism: Develops a sensitive potentiometric resolved ratiometric photoelectrochemical aptasensor for the detection of E. coli.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved an extremely low detection limit (LOD) of 0.66 cfu/mL and showed a wide linear range (2.9 cfu/mL to 2.9 × 10(6) cfu/mL).

Title: Carbon nanotube-based aptasensor for sensitive electrochemical detection of whole-cell Salmonella
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an amino-modified aptasensor using MWCNTs-deposited ITO electrode for the detection of Salmonella.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: It possesses a linear range from 10 mV/s to 90 mV /s, and the detection limit was 5.5 × 10(1) cfu/mL and 6.7 × 10(1) cfu/mL for S. Enteritidis and S. Typhimurium, respectively.

Title: Fast and Sensitive Detection of Salmonella in Milk Samples Using Aptamer-Functionalized Magnetic Silica Solid Phase and MCM-41-Aptamer Gate System
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer-gated MCM-41 silica system (Fe3O4@SiO2@pGMA and MCM-41 particles) to detect S. enterica in food samples.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The linear range is from 2000 CFU/mL to 104 CFU/mL in milk, with the LOD of 2336 cells.

Title: Sensitive and specific detection of clinical bacteria via vancomycin-modified Fe3O4@Au nanoparticles and aptamer-functionalized SERS tags
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a dual-recognition SERS platform using vancomycin-modified Fe3O4@Au magnetic nanoparticles (Fe3O4@Au-Van MNPs) for the detection of E. coli and S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The LOD of the platform was 20 cells/mL for S. aureus, with a capture efficiency of up to 88.89% within 15 min.

Title: Sensitive and specific detection of clinical bacteria via vancomycin-modified Fe3O4@Au nanoparticles and aptamer-functionalized SERS tags
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a dual-recognition SERS platform using vancomycin-modified Fe3O4@Au magnetic nanoparticles (Fe3O4@Au-Van MNPs) for the detection of E. coli and S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The LOD of the platform was 50 cells/mL for E. coli, and capture efficiency reached 74.96% within 15 min.

Title: Aptamer immobilization on amino-functionalized metal-organic frameworks: an ultrasensitive platform for the electrochemical diagnostic of Escherichia coli O157:H7
Objective/Mechanism: Electrochemical biosensor based on amino-functionalized metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for detection of Escherichia coli O157:H7.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display linear range of 2.1×10(1) to 2.1×10(7) CFU/mL with a LOQ of 21 CFU/mL and LOD of 2 CFU/mL.

Title: Staggered Target SELEX, a novel approach to isolate non-cross-reactive aptamer for detection of SEA by apta-qPCR
Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers by ST-SELEX and use them for the detection of SEA via apta-Real-time PCR (apta-qPCR).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The limit of detection (LOD) was 146.67 fM.

Title: Construction and application of an electrochemical biosensor based on an endotoxin aptamer
Objective/Mechanism: An electrochemical aptasensor was developed using an aptamer assembled on a gold electrode surface using 3-mercaptopropionic acid (MPA) as an intermediate linker to detect endotoxin.

Title: Construction and application of an electrochemical biosensor based on an endotoxin aptamer
Objective/Mechanism: An electrochemical aptasensor was developed using an aptamer assembled on a gold electrode surface using 3-mercaptopropionic acid (MPA) as an intermediate linker to detect endotoxin.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Showed a low detection limit of 0.001 EU/mL and a linear range of 0.001–1 EU/mL.
Stability: The biosensor maintained a steady EIS response value after 1 week of storage in the PBS (10 mM, pH 7.4) at 4°C, and the response value still occupied 90%.

Title: Gold atomic cluster mediated electrochemical aptasensor for the detection of lipopolysaccharide
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer immobilized gold atomic cluster mediated, ultrasensitive electrochemical biosensor (Apt/AuAC/Au) for LPS detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a detection of LPS down to 7.94 × 10–21 M level with a wide dynamic range from 0.01 attomolar to 1 pM.
Stability: The Apt/AuAC/Au electrode offers excellent stability when stored at 4°C for 1 week, with 95.54% of the signal retained.

Title: Dual-aptamer-based voltammetric biosensor for the Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigen MPT64 by using a gold electrode modified with a peroxidase loaded composite consisting of gold nanoparticles and a Zr(IV)/terephthalate metal-organic framework
Objective/Mechanism: A sandwich-like dual-aptamer strategy employing an ultrasensitive aptasensor for the voltammetric determination of M. tuberculosis. antigen MPT64 in human serum.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved an ultrasensitive detection limit of 10 fg/mL and a wide linear response range from 0.02 to 1000 pg/mL.

Title: Dual-aptamer-based voltammetric biosensor for the Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigen MPT64 by using a gold electrode modified with a peroxidase loaded composite consisting of gold nanoparticles and a Zr(IV)/terephthalate metal-organic framework
Objective/Mechanism: A sandwich-like dual-aptamer strategy where two different aptamers are immobilized on a gold electrode to synergistically bind the target MPT64 protein
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved an ultrasensitive detection limit of 10 fg/mL and a wide linear response range from 0.02 to 1000 pg/mL.

Title: New colorimetric aptasensor for rapid on-site detection of Campylobacter jejuni and Campylobacter coli in chicken carcass samples
Target Organism: Campylobacter Jejuni (ATCC 33560, NCTC11168, 2 human isolates, and 3 food isolates)
Objective/Mechanism: A 2-stage label-free aptasensing platform was developed to detect C. jejuni and C. coli.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Detection limit (LOD) of 7.2×10^5 CFU/mL and linear range from 10(5) to 10(8) CFU/mL for C. jejuni.

Title: New colorimetric aptasensor for rapid on-site detection of Campylobacter jejuni and Campylobacter coli in chicken carcass samples
Objective/Mechanism: Aptamers normally adsorb to gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) to protect them from salt-induced aggregation.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Detection limit (LOD) of 5.6×10^5 CFU/mL with a strong correlation (from 10(5) to 10(8) CFU/mL) for C. coli.

Title: Aptamer based voltammetric biosensor for Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigen ESAT-6 using a nanohybrid material composed of reduced graphene oxide and a metal-organic framework
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a voltammetric aptasensor employing P-MOF-rGO nanohybrid as the sensitive sensing platform for ultrasensitive detection of ESAT-6.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Linear range: 1.0×10(−4) to 2.0×10(2) ng/mL and Limit of Detection (LOD): 3.3×10(−5) ng/mL.
Stability: Compared with the initial current response, the aptsensor response decreased only about 3.5% after 50 cycles’ continuous CV scans.

Title: Label-free aptasensors based on fluorescent screening assays for the detection of Salmonella typhimurium
Objective/Mechanism: A label-free fluorescent aptasensor was developed for the detection of Salmonella typhimurium using SYBR Green I.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a linear range of approximately 1530-96938 CFU/mL and a detection limit of 733 CFU/mL.

Title: Label-free aptasensors based on fluorescent screening assays for the detection of Salmonella typhimurium
Objective/Mechanism: An aptasensor based on FRET between Rhodamine B and gold nanoparticles for the detection of Salmonella typhimurium was developed.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved concentrations ranging from 1530 to 96938 CFU/mL, with a detection limit of 464 CFU/mL.

Title: Ω-Shaped Fiber-Optic Probe-Based Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance Biosensor for Real-Time Detection of Salmonella Typhimurium
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer-immobilized Ω-shaped fiber-optic localized surface plasmon resonance (FOLSPR) biosensor for S. Typhimurium detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved high detection sensitivity for S. Typhimurium down to 128 CFU/mL within a linear range from 5 × 10(2) to 1 × 10(8) CFU/mL.

Title: Nanoporous gold as a suitable substrate for preparation of a new sensitive electrochemical aptasensor for detection of Salmonella typhimurium
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a label-free electrochemical aptasensor based on nanoporous gold (NPG/Au/GCE) for the detection of Salmonella typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Capable of detecting S. typhimurium in a wide linear dynamic range 6.5 × 10(2) to 6.5 × 10(8) CFU/mL with a LOD of 1 CFU/mL.

Title: Culture-free, highly sensitive, quantitative detection of bacteria from minimally processed samples using fluorescence imaging by smartphone
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a smartphone-based detection using aptamer-functionalized fluorescent magnetic nanoparticles (FMNPs) for Staphylococcus aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Showed a minimum detectable concentration as low as 10 cfu/ml in a peanut milk sample within 10 min.

Title: Magnetism-Resolved Separation and Fluorescence Quantification for Near-Simultaneous Detection of Multiple Pathogens
Objective/Mechanism: Aptamer-modified fluorescent-magnetic multifunctional nanoprobes (apt-FMNPs) for near-simultaneous detection of multiple pathogens.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The detection limits were 100 cfu/mL in milk, 80 cfu/mL in human serum, and 80 cfu/mL in human urine for E. coli.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): Bacterial viability remained about 100% during incubation with apt-FMNPs nanoprobes at successive incubation time points of 0, 0.5, 1, 3, 6, 12, and 18 h.

Title: Magnetism-Resolved Separation and Fluorescence Quantification for Near-Simultaneous Detection of Multiple Pathogens
Objective/Mechanism: Aptamer-modified fluorescent-magnetic multifunctional nanoprobes (apt-FMNPs) for near-simultaneous detection of multiple pathogens.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The detection limits of 150 cfu/mL in milk, 120 cfu/mL in human serum, and 120 cfu/mL in human urine for S. typ.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): Bacterial viability remained about 100% during incubation with apt-FMNPs nanoprobes at successive incubation time points of 0, 0.5, 1, 3, 6, 12, and 18 h.

Title: Theranostic Application of a Novel G-Quadruplex-Forming DNA Aptamer Targeting Malate Synthase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis
Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers that bind to and inhibit the MS enzyme activity, thereby blocking bacterial entry into host cells.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Inhibited MS activity with an IC₅₀ of 251.1 nM; Ki of 230 nM; inhibited M. tb invasion into human THP-1 monocytic cells.

Title: Theranostic Application of a Novel G-Quadruplex-Forming DNA Aptamer Targeting Malate Synthase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis

Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Inhibition of MS activity, the aptamers were ranked as MS10 (IC50 of 275.6 nM, Ki of 270 nM) > MS5 > MS20 > MS4 > MS6.

Title: C4-HSL aptamers for blocking quorum sensing and inhibiting biofilm formation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa and its structure prediction and analysis
Target: C4-HSL of the rhl system quorum sensing molecule
Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers that inhibit biofilm formation and quorum sensing.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Biofilm formation by P. aeruginosa was reduced by about 1/3.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): Aptamers caused no effect on bacterial growth.

Title: Aptamer-mediated colorimetric and electrochemical detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa utilizing peroxidase-mimic activity of gold NanoZyme
Objective/Mechanism: Aptamer-mediated tunable NanoZyme colorimetric and electrochemical sensors for the detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Possess a detection limit of the electrochemical sensor of ~ 60 CFU/mL in water within 10 min.

Title: Aptamer-based fluorometric determination of Salmonella Typhimurium using Fe3O4 magnetic separation and CdTe quantum dots
Objective/Mechanism: Develop an aptamer-based (Apt-MNPs) fluorescence assay for the determination of Salmonella Typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibit a linear range of 10 to 10(10) cfu/mL with LOD of 1 cfu/mL within 2 h, and is successfully applied to the analysis of spiked food samples with good recoveries from 90% to 105%.

Title: Rapid Detection of Mycoplasma-Infected Cells by an ssDNA Aptamer Probe
Objective/Mechanism: Develop an aptamer probe for the rapid detection of mycoplasma-infected cells.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Mycoplasma-positive cells showed a strong signal, but no signal was detected in the mycoplasma-negative cells.

Title: A new aptamer/polyadenylated DNA interdigitated gold electrode piezoelectric sensor for rapid detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a piezoelectric sensor (Au IDE-MSPQC) based on magnetic bead/aptamer/polyadenylated-DNA for the detection of P. aeruginosa.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The limits of detection (LOD) of the method were as low as 9 CFU/mL in buffer and 52 CFU/mL in a simulated blood sample.

Title: Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopic single step detection of Vibrio parahaemolyticus using gold coated polydimethylsiloxane as the active substrate and aptamer modified gold nanoparticles
Objective/Mechanism: Aptamer-based SERS method using Au-PDMS film for the detection of V. parahaemolyticus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The detection limit is 12 cfu/mL with a wide linear range from 1.2 × 10(2) to 1.2 × 10(6) cfu/mL.

Title: Vertical capacitance aptasensors for real-time monitoring of bacterial growth and antibiotic susceptibility in blood
Objective/Mechanism: Vertical-type aptamer-functionalized sensor (aptasensor) for monitoring bacterial growth and antibiotic susceptibility in blood in real-time.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Detect bacteria growth in blood at 10(0)-10(3) CFU/mL in real-time within 12 hours, and the MIC for E. coli was approximately 0.1 and 1 μg/mL for gentamicin and amikacin, respectively.

Title: Vertical capacitance aptasensors for real-time monitoring of bacterial growth and antibiotic susceptibility in blood
Objective/Mechanism: Vertical-type aptamer-functionalized sensor (aptasensor) for monitoring bacterial growth and antibiotic susceptibility in blood in real-time.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Detect bacteria growth in blood at 10(0)-10(3) CFU/mL in real-time within 12 hours and the MIC for S. aureus was approximately 1 and 0.1 μg/mL for gentamicin and amikacin, respectively,

Title: Vertical capacitance aptasensors for real-time monitoring of bacterial growth and antibiotic susceptibility in blood
Objective/Mechanism: Vertical-type aptamer-functionalized sensor (aptasensor) for monitoring bacterial growth and antibiotic susceptibility in blood in real-time.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Detect bacteria growth in blood at 10(0)-10(3) CFU/mL in real-time within 12 hours and the MIC for P. aeruginosa was approximately 1 μg/mL for both gentamicin and amikacin.

Title: A nano-sized chitosan particle based electrochemical aptasensor for sensitive detection of P. aeruginosa
Objective/Mechanism: Develop an aptasensor based on a glassy carbon electrode (GCE) modified with nano-sized chitosan particles (NCs) for sensitive and simultaneous detection of P. aeruginosa.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Displayed a low detection limit of 3 CFU/mL, wide linearity of 10(1)–10(7) CFU/mL and a recovery rate from 93.2% to 124%.

Title: Development of a Sensitive Diagnostic Device Based on Zeolitic Imidazolate Frameworks-8 Using Ferrocene–Graphene Oxide as Electroactive Indicator for Pseudomonas aeruginosa Detection
Objective/Mechanism: An electrochemical biosensor (Fc-GO/Apt/HZIFs-8/GCE ) based on aptamers immobilized in engineered zeolitic imidazolate Framework-8 (ZIFs-8) for the detection of P. aeruginosa in human urine samples.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibits a wide linear dynamic range (from 1.2 × 10(1) to 1.2 × 10(7) CFU/mL) with a low detection limit of 1 CFU/mL.

Title: Dual-aptamers labeled polydopamine-polyethyleneimine copolymer dots assisted engineering a fluorescence biosensor for sensitive detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in food samples
Objective/Mechanism: A dual aptamer labelled PDA-PEI copolymer dots-based biosensor for detection and quantification of P. aeruginosa.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The LOD of P. aeruginosa is as low as 1 cfu/mL with a linear range from 10(1)–10(7) cfu/mL in 1.5h.

Title: Dual-aptamers labeled polydopamine-polyethyleneimine copolymer dots assisted engineering a fluorescence biosensor for sensitive detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in food samples
Objective/Mechanism: A dual aptamer labelled PDA-PEI copolymer dots-based biosensor for detection and quantification of P. aeruginosa.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The LOD of P. aeruginosa is as low as 1 cfu/mL with a linear range from 10(1)–10(7) cfu/mL in 1.5h.

Title: A novel enzyme-free electrochemical biosensor for rapid detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa based on high catalytic Cu-ZrMOF and conductive Super P
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a Cu-ZrMOF@Aptamer@DNA nanocomposite-based enzyme-free electrochemical biosensor to detect P. aeruginosa.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibit a wide linearity range of 10-10(6) CFU/mL and a low limit of detection of 2 CFU/mL within 120 min.
Stability: The biosensor had acceptable storage stability (98.1% and 83.9%) within 7 days of storage at 4°C.

Title: Impedimetric aptasensor for Pseudomonas aeruginosa by using a glassy carbon electrode modified with silver nanoparticles
Objective/Mechanism: Develop an aptasensor based on an immobilised NH2-aptamer that was covalently attached to the AgNP/GCE surface for the detection of P. aeruginosa.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The impedance increases on going from 10(2) to 10(7) CFU/mL concentrations of P. aeruginosa, and the detection limit is 33 CFU/mL.

Title: A reduced graphene oxide-titanium dioxide nanocomposite based electrochemical aptasensor for rapid and sensitive detection of Salmonella enterica
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a rGO-TiO2 electrochemical aptasensor for the detection of Salmonella bacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited high sensitivity with a wide detection range (10(8) to 10(1) cfu/mL), a low detection limit of 10(1) cfu/mL.
Stability: Showed good durability up to 21 days with a 10% decrease in signal after 30 days of non-use.

Title: A competitive enzyme linked aptasensor with rolling circle amplification (ELARCA) assay for colorimetric detection of Listeria monocytogenes
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an enzyme-linked aptasensor with rolling circle amplification (ELARCA) assay for the detection of L. monocytogenes.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Showed a limit of detection (LOD) of 4.6 × 10(2) CFU/mL in pure culture, and in fresh lettuce showed an LOD of 6.1 × 10(3) CFU/g.

Title: Fluorometric determination of lipopolysaccharides via changes of the graphene oxide-enhanced fluorescence polarization caused by truncated aptamers
Target Organism: Salmonella Typhimurium (S. Typhimurium), Escherichia Coli (E. Coli) 055:B5 and Pseudomonas Aeruginosa 10
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer-based graphene oxide-based fluorescence polarization assay to detect LPSs from S. typhimurium, P. aeruginosa 10 and E. coli 055:B5.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Detection limits (3σ/S) obtained within 30 minutes using LA27 with respect to LPS, Pa-LPS, and Ecoli-LPS were 38.7, 88.0, and 154 ng/mL, respectively.

Objective/Mechanism: A biosensor using Dual-Apt and cut-assisted rolling circle amplification (CA-RCA) for rapid and visualized detection of Vibrio parahaemolyticus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Shows a good linear correlation in the range from 10(6) to 10 CFU/mL and LOD as low as 10 CFU/mL (g) in real food samples.

Title: Dual-recognition surface-enhanced Raman scattering(SERS)biosensor for pathogenic bacteria detection by using vancomycin-SERS tags and aptamer-Fe3O4@Au
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a dual-recognition SERS biosensor using Vancomycin-Au@MBA and aptamer-Fe3O4@Au for the detection of pathogenic bacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: A detection limit of 3 cells/mL with a wide dynamic linear range from 10 to 10(7) cells/mL can be achieved within 50 min.

Objective/Mechanism: Identify an aptamer against and develop a colorimetric aptasensor based on magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) and G4 DNAzyme to detect V. parahemolyticus in contaminated salmon samples.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibits a wide linear detection range (from 10(2) to 10(7) cfu/mL), and the detection limit could be as low as 10 cfu/mL.

Title: Colorimetric detection and typing of E. coli lipopolysaccharides based on a dual aptamer-functionalized gold nanoparticle probe
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a dual aptamer-based colorimetric method for the identification of E.coli LPS.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Can detect LPS in concentrations between 2.5 and 20 μg/mL and with a 1 μg/mL detection limit.

Title: Colorimetric detection and typing of E. coli lipopolysaccharides based on a dual aptamer-functionalized gold nanoparticle probe
Target Organism: Escherichia Coli (E. Coli) O111:B4 and O111:B5
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a dual aptamer-based colorimetric method for the identification of E.coli LPS.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Can detect LPS in concentrations between 2.5 and 20 μg/mL and with a 1 μg/mL detection limit.

Title: A novel aptamer-based test for the rapid and accurate diagnosis of pleural tuberculosis
Objective/Mechanism: Aptamer-Linked Immobilized Sorbent Assay (ALISA) was developed to detect pleural TB (pTB).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Detects pTB with ~93% sensitivity and ~98% specificity.

Title: Structural switching electrochemical DNA aptasensor for the rapid diagnosis of tuberculous meningitis
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a structural switching electrochemical aptasensor using methylene blue (MB) and an aptamer for the detection of HspX in CSF samples for the diagnosis of TBM.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Can detect as low as 10 pg HspX in CSF with ~95% sensitivity and ~97.5% specificity in ≤30 minutes.

Title: A transcription aptasensor: amplified, label-free and culture-independent detection of foodborne pathogens via light-up RNA aptamers
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a transcription aptasensor by using a light-up RNA aptamer for culture-free detection of intact foodborne pathogens.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The dynamic range was 10(2)-10(6) CFU/mL, and the LOD of the transcription aptasensor was estimated to be 77.0 CFU/mL.

Title: Ultrasensitive Fluorometric Angling Determination of Staphylococcus aureus in Vitro and Fluorescence Imaging in Vivo Using Carbon Dots with Full-Color Emission
Objective/Mechanism: An ultrasensitive magnetic fluorescence aptasensor was designed using Fe3O4/CD for the separation and detection of S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The FRET-based aptasensor achieved a wide linear range of 50–10(7) CFU/mL and a detection limit of 8 CFU/mL.

Title: Rapid and label-free detection of Brucella melitensis in milk and milk products using an aptasensor
Objective/Mechanism: A QCM-aptasensor [Fe3O4 @SiO2 @p(PEG-MA-GMA)] was developed for the determination of B. melitensis from food samples.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The detection limits of the QCM aptasensor were in the range 1.0(2)–1.0(7) CFU/mL, with recoveries up to 79% and LOD of 100 CFU/mL.

Title: Aptamer Affinity-Bead Mediated Capture and Displacement of Gram-Negative Bacteria Using Acoustophoresis
Objective/Mechanism: Develop aptamer-modified microbeads and an acoustophoresis method for capturing and displacing gram-negative bacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: It achieved high recovery (up to 98%) and high purity (up to 99.5%).

Title: Detection of Gram-negative bacterial outer membrane vesicles using DNA aptamers
Target Organism: Gram-negative Bacteria (Escherichia Coli (E. Coli) DH5α, Escherichia Coli (E. Coli) K12, and Serratia Marcescens)
Objective/Mechanism: Isolated aptamers against multiple Gram-negative bacterial species and developed an aptamer-based detection tool (ELAA) towards bacterial secretory cargo released from the outer membranes of Gram-negative bacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Can detect as low as 25 ng/mL of bacterial OMVs, and dissociation constants of GN6 to OMVs derived from E. coli DH5α, E. coli K12 and S. marcescens were 0.13 ± 0.01 μg/ml, 3.70 ± 0.98 μg/ml and 0.23 ± 0.16 μg/ml, respectively.
Kd value: 29.94 ± 2.49 nM (for E. coli DH5α), 59.70 ± 10.89 nM (for E. coli K12) and 38.98 ± 6.46 nM (for S. marcescens)

Title: Detection of Gram-negative bacterial outer membrane vesicles using DNA aptamers
Target Organism: Gram-negative Bacteria (Escherichia Coli (E. Coli) DH5α, Escherichia Coli (E. Coli) K12, and Serratia Marcescens)
Objective/Mechanism: Isolated aptamers against multiple Gram-negative bacterial species and developed an aptamer-based detection tool towards bacterial secretory cargo released from the outer membranes of Gram-negative bacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: GN12 was 3.6 times higher in binding to 10(8) cells of Gram-negative bacteria than to Gram-positive bacteria tested.
Kd value: 20.36 ± 2.38 nM (for E. coli DH5α), 24.80 ± 3.98 nM (for E. coli K12) and 53.83 ± 17.70 nM (for S. marcescens)

Title: Rapid identification and quantitation of the viable cells of Lactobacillus casei in fermented dairy products using an aptamer-based strategy powered by a novel cell-SELEX protocol
Objective/Mechanism: An aptamer-based strategy using PEG and chitosan-modified graphene oxide, with complementary ring-mediated RCA, was developed for qualitative and quantitative detection of viable L. casei in dairy products.

Title: Rapid identification and quantitation of the viable cells of Lactobacillus casei in fermented dairy products using an aptamer-based strategy powered by a novel cell-SELEX protocol
Objective/Mechanism: An aptamer-based strategy using PEG and chitosan-modified graphene oxide, with complementary ring-mediated RCA, was developed for qualitative and quantitative detection of viable L. casei in dairy products.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a detection limit of 10(5) cfu/mL and selective detection of L. casei in commercial dairy drinks, with a dynamic range of 10(5) to 10(9) cfu/mL.

Title: Rapid identification and quantitation of the viable cells of Lactobacillus casei in fermented dairy products using an aptamer-based strategy powered by a novel cell-SELEX protocol
Objective/Mechanism: An aptamer-based strategy using PEG and chitosan-modified graphene oxide, with complementary ring-mediated RCA, was developed for qualitative and quantitative detection of viable L. casei in dairy products.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a detection limit of 10(5) cfu/mL and selective detection of L. casei in commercial dairy drinks, with a dynamic range of 10(5) to 10(9) cfu/mL.

Title: A glassy carbon electrode modified with reduced graphene oxide and gold nanoparticles for electrochemical aptasensing of lipopolysaccharides from Escherichia coli bacteria
Objective/Mechanism: An electrochemical aptasensor immobilized on a GCE modified with reduced graphene oxide and gold nanoparticles (RGO/AuNPs) was developed for the voltammetric determination of LPS from E. coli 055:B5.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Limit of Detection (LOD) of 1 fg/mL (using Mg/CQD media) or 30 fg/mL (using hexacyanoferrate).

Title: A sandwich-type electrochemical aptasensor for Mycobacterium tuberculosis MPT64 antigen detection using C60NPs decorated N-CNTs/GO nanocomposite coupled with conductive PEI-functionalized metal-organic framework
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a sandwich-type electrochemical aptasensor using (C60NPs-N-CNTs/GO) for the detection of MPT64 antigen.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Showed a wide linear range from 1 fg/mL to 1 ng/mL with a limit of detection (LOD) as low as 0.33 fg/mL.
Stability: Oxidation current remains 94.5% of the initial level after 80 cycles, and peak current remains approximately 98.7%, 93.5%, and 90.6% of the initial peak current after 7, 14, and 21 days, respectively.

Title: A sandwich-type electrochemical aptasensor for Mycobacterium tuberculosis MPT64 antigen detection using C60NPs decorated N-CNTs/GO nanocomposite coupled with conductive PEI-functionalized metal-organic framework
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a sandwich-type electrochemical aptasensor using (C60NPs-N-CNTs/GO) for the detection of MPT64 antigen.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Showed a wide linear range from 1 fg/mL to 1 ng/mL with a limit of detection (LOD) as low as 0.33 fg/mL.
Stability: Oxidation current remains 94.5% of the initial level after 80 cycles, and peak current remains approximately 98.7%, 93.5%, and 90.6% of the initial peak current after 7, 14, and 21 days, respectively.

Title: Aptamer-based SERS biosensor for whole cell analytical detection of E. coli O157:H7
Objective/Mechanism: SERS-based aptasensor using 4-aminothiophenol-gold nanoparticle complexes was developed for the detection of E. coli O157:H7.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Low concentrations of E. coli O157:H7 were detected and quantified within 20 min in both pure culture (∼10(1) CFU/mL) and ground beef samples (∼10(2) CFU/mL), and a linear range from 10(2) to 10(6) CFU/mL.

Title: Development of an Electrochemical Biosensor for Rapid and Effective Detection of Pathogenic Escherichia coli in Licorice Extract
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer-based electrochemical biosensor for the rapid detection of E. coli in liquorice extract.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Concentrations ranging from 5.0 × 10^2 CFU/mL to 5.0 × 10^7 CFU/mL exhibited a linear trend, with a detection limit of 80 CFU/mL.

Title: Electrochemical determination of Salmonella typhimurium by using aptamer-loaded gold nanoparticles and a composite prepared from a metal-organic framework (type UiO-67) and graphene
Objective/Mechanism: An aptamer-based assay based on a metal-organic framework-graphene composite of type UiO-67/GR and an aptamer-gold nanoparticles-horseradish peroxidase (Apt-AuNP-HRP) conjugate is described for the determination of S.typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Linear detection range from 2 × 10(1) – 2 × 10(8) cfu/mL and a lower detection limit of 5 cfu/mL.
Stability: 91.3% of the original current is retained after storage at 4°C for 14 days with the modified electrodes, allowing monitoring of 2 × 10(5) cfu/mL S. typhimurium.

Title: Polyadenine-mediated Immobilization of Aptamers on a Gold Substrate for the Direct Detection of Bacterial Pathogens
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a SPR-based aptasenor using polyadenine-mediated immobilization of aptamers on a gold substrate for the detection of E. coli or S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The detection limit of the current SPR aptasensor is 1 x 10(5) CFU/mL for E. coli.

Title: Polyadenine-mediated Immobilization of Aptamers on a Gold Substrate for the Direct Detection of Bacterial Pathogens
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a SPR-based aptasenor using polyadenine-mediated immobilization of aptamers on a gold substrate for the detection of E. coli or S. aureus.

Title: Polyadenine-mediated Immobilization of Aptamers on a Gold Substrate for the Direct Detection of Bacterial Pathogens
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a SPR-based aptasenor using polyadenine-mediated immobilization of aptamers on a gold substrate for the detection of E. coli or S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The detection limit of the current SPR aptasensors is 1 x 10(6) CFU/mL for S. aureus.

Objective/Mechanism: Developed a SPR-based aptasenor using polyadenine-mediated immobilization of aptamers on a gold substrate for the detection of E. coli or S. aureus.

Objective/Mechanism: Developed a SPR-based aptasenor using polyadenine-mediated immobilization of aptamers on a gold substrate for the detection of E. coli or S. aureus.

Objective/Mechanism: Developed a SPR-based aptasenor using polyadenine-mediated immobilization of aptamers on a gold substrate for the detection of E. coli or S. aureus.

Title: An electrochemical aptasensor for staphylococcal enterotoxin B detection based on reduced graphene oxide and gold nano-urchins
Objective/Mechanism: An electrochemical aptasensor was developed using a screen-printed electrode modified with reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and gold nano-urchins (AuNUs) for the detection of SEB.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: A wide linear range of 5.0–500.0 fM was observed, with a detection limit of 0.21 fM.

Title: A label-free impedimetric aptasensor for the detection of Bacillus anthracis spore simulant
Target: B. anthracis spore simulant (B. cereus spore 14579)
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an impedimetric DNA-based aptasensor based on an aptamer immolized on a gold screen-printed electrode for a single-step detection of B. cereus spores.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Spores were detected with a linear range between 10(4) CFU/ml and 5 × 10(6) CFU/ml and a detection limit of 3 × 10(3) CFU/ml.

Title: Electrochemical aptasensor using optimized surface chemistry for the detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis secreted protein MPT64 in human serum
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an electrochemical aptasensor using thiol PEGylated aptamer HS-(CH2)6-OP(O)2O-(CH2CH2O)6-TTTTT-aptamer and 6-mercaptohexanol for the detection of MPT64.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: A spiked human serum sample displays a limit of detection of 81 pM in 30 minutes with the long linker aptamer/MCH.

Title: Screening of highly-specific aptamers and their applications in paper-based microfluidic chips for rapid diagnosis of multiple bacteria
Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers and develop a dual-aptamer, NC-based microfluidic chip for fast diagnosis of three common nosocomial bacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: LOD was estimated to be 10(3) for AB.

Title: Screening of highly-specific aptamers and their applications in paper-based microfluidic chips for rapid diagnosis of multiple bacteria
Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers and develop a dual-aptamer, NC-based microfluidic chip for fast diagnosis of three common nosocomial bacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: LOD was estimated to be 10(4) for EC.

Title: Screening of highly-specific aptamers and their applications in paper-based microfluidic chips for rapid diagnosis of multiple bacteria
Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers and develop a dual-aptamer, NC-based microfluidic chip for fast diagnosis of three common nosocomial bacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: LOD was estimated to be 10(5) CFU/μL for MRSA.

Title: Inkjet Printed Nanopatterned Aptamer-Based Sensors for Improved Optical Detection of Foodborne Pathogens
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an inkjet-printed nanopatterned aptamer-based sensor for optical detection of E. coli O157:H7.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a LOD of 25 CFU/mL in pure culture and 233 CFU/mL in ground beef.

Title: Aptamer surface functionalization of microfluidic devices using dendrimers as multi-handled templates and its application in sensitive detections of foodborne pathogenic bacteria
Objective/Mechanism: A microfluidic system using a dendrimer-aptamer modified surface was developed for sensitive detection of E. coli O157:H7.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The G7-apatamer modified detection system achieved a low limit of detection of 10(2) cells/mL.

Title: Naked-eyes detection of Shigella flexneri in food samples based on a novel gold nanoparticle-based colorimetric aptasensor
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a colourimetric aptasensor based on an aptamer and gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) for the visual detection of Sh. flexneri.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a linear range from 10(2) to 10(6) CFU/mL with the detection limit of 80 CFU/mL, and the detection time was 20 min or less.

Title: Functional chimera aptamer and molecular beacon based fluorescent detection of Staphylococcus aureus with strand displacement-target recycling amplification
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a fluorescent detection of S. aureus based on a functional chimaera and a molecular beacon.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a broad concentration range from 80 CFU/mL to 8 × 10(6) CFU/mL and the detection limit of 39 CFU/mL.

Title: Engineering DNA-Nanozyme Interfaces for Rapid Detection of Dental Bacteria
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a DNA-engineered nanozyme interface using aptamers for the detection of dental bacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The detection limit is 12 CFU/mL, and the linear range is 0 to 10(9) CFU/mL.

Title: Single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) Aptamer targeting SipA protein inhibits Salmonella Enteritidis invasion of intestinal epithelial cells
Objective/Mechanism: Identify an aptamer targeting the SipA protein and interfere with the function of effector proteins to prevent host cell invasion.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: 70% and 37.7% inhibition ratios against adhesion and invasion of S. enteritidis TM 6 to Caco-2 cells, 45.71% and 39.5% against those of S. enteritidis TM 68, respectively.

Title: Inhibitory effects of aptamer targeted teicoplanin encapsulated PLGA nanoparticles for Staphylococcus aureus strains
Target Organism: Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) susceptible strains and MRSA
Objective/Mechanism: Aptamer-PLGA nanoparticles (Apt-teicoplanin-PLGA NPs) for the delivery of teicoplanin antibiotic.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: MICs of teicoplanin decreased by 32- and 64-fold for susceptible strains and MRSA strains, respectively.

Objective/Mechanism: Interfering with the biofilm formation via abolishing the motility and quorum sensing.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited the highest biofilm inhibition towards EPEC K1.1 shown by lowest OD value of 0.126.

Title: Electrical antimicrobial susceptibility testing based on aptamer-functionalized capacitance sensor array for clinical isolates
Target Organism: Escherichia Coli (E. Coli) (U433, U556-ESBL, B12327, U5307, U6267-ESBL)
Objective/Mechanism: Electrical AST (e-AST) chips composed of 60 aptamer-functionalized capacitance sensors to detect bacteria and measure the antibiotic susceptibility to 11 antibiotics at five different concentrations.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The discrepancies between e-AST and BMD tests were estimated to be 2.20% mE, 0.38% ME, and 0.38%, which are lower than the FDA requirements (mE ≤ 10%, ME ≤ 3%, and VME ≤ 1.5%).

Objective/Mechanism: Dual-functional technology based on aptamer and CRISPR-Cas12a-assisted RCA for detection of MRSA.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Fluorescence intensity shows a linear correlation with the logarithm of MRSA concentration, ranging from 10(6) to 10(2) CFU/mL, spanning six orders of magnitude.

Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Within 30 minutes, a limit of detection of only 100 CFU/reaction and a range of 10^2 to 10^5 CFU/reaction was obtained.

Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Detects V.P in the range of 10–10(9) cfu/mL with an LOD of 3 cfu/mL and within only 20 min.
Stability: No significant difference in the measured blank and signals was observed over 3 months with aptasensor, when 91.3% of the initial signal was obtained.

Title: Simple Colorimetric Assay for Vibrio parahaemolyticus Detection Using Aptamer-Functionalized Nanoparticles
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a visual colorimetric assay using aptamer-conjugated MNPs and AuNPs for the detection of V. parahaemolyticus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Shows a linear range of 10-10(6) cfu/mL, with a limit of detection of 2.4 cfu/mL.

Objective/Mechanism: Developed an eye-based aptasensor (EA-Sensor) for the detection of E.coli O157:H7.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a linear range of 500–5 × 10(7) CFU/mL and LOD of 250 CFU/mL and 400 CFU/mL for buffered and milk samples.

Title: Ultrasensitive detection of Listeria monocytogenes using solid-state electrochemiluminescence biosensing based on the quenching effect of ferrocene on ruthenium pyridine

Objective/Mechanism: QCM-based aptasensor for the detection of pathogenic bacteria Listeria innocua.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The achieved limit of detection was approximately 1.6 × 10(3) CFU/mL and broad range of 5 × 10(3)-10(6) CFU/mL.

Title: Development of a fluorescence aptasensor for rapid and sensitive detection of Listeria monocytogenes in food
Objective/Mechanism: A fluorescence aptasensor based on aptamer-UCNP and aptamer-MNP complex was developed for the detection of L. monocytogenes.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: A low limit of detection of 8 cfu/mL was estimated from the range of 68 to 68 × 10(6) cfu/mL.

Objective/Mechanism: A fluorescent aptasensor based on MB-apt-cDNA duplex for S. aureus in milk samples.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibits a broad linear range from 7 to 7 × 10(7) CFU/mL, with a detection limit of 1.7 CFU/mL for S. aureus.

Objective/Mechanism: Developed a fluorescent aptasensor based on aptamer-modified SiC quantum dots (DNA-SiC QDs) for the determination of Proteus mirabilis.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The linear range is from 10(3) to 10(8) CFU/mL, and the limit of detection is 526 CFU/mL.

Title: Rapid and sensitive detection of Salmonella Typhimurium using nickel nanowire bridge for electrochemical impedance amplification
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an electrochemical aptasensor using an aptamer-coated gold interdigitated microelectrode and antibody-modified NiNWs to detect Salmonella typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: This electrochemical aptasensor quantitatively detected Salmonella at concentrations ranging from 10(2) to 10(6) CFU/mL within 2 h, with a detection limit of 80 CFU/mL.

Title: CdS quantum dots/Au nanoparticles/ZnO nanowire array for self-powered photoelectrochemical detection of Escherichia coli O157:H7
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a photoelectrochemical (PEC) platform (CdS QDs/Au NPs/ZnO NWs) for the detection of E. coli O157:H7.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a wide linear range of 10-10(7) CFU/mL with the detection limit as low as 1.125 CFU/mL.

Outcome/Inhibitory effect: After treatment with 5 μM N4-AgNCs/Apt-G, a significantly reduced number of colonies was observed. At the lowest inhibitory concentration of 6.25 μM, the number of colonies decreased by only 4-fold, which is significantly less than the 7-fold reduction observed at 5 μM.
