Title: Efficient Eradication of Bacterial Biofilms with Highly Specific Graphene-Based Nanocomposite Sheets
Objective/Mechanism: ICG@GO-Apt nanosheets for eradication of biofilm associated with Salmonella Typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Shows an efficient biofilm elimination with an efficiency of greater than 99.99% in an abscess formation model.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): ICG@GO-Apt NSs had almost no cytotoxicity to HEK 293 cells, with more than 90% and lacked hemolytic activities.

Title: An aptamer biosensor based dual signal amplification system for the detection of salmonella typhimurium
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a signal-cascade-amplification method named “immuno-HCR-SERS” for the detection of S. typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Highly sensitive detection showing a linear range from 10 to 10(5) CFU/mL, with a limit of detection (LOD) of 6 CFU/mL in 3.5 h.

Title: A Colorimetric Strategy Based on Aptamer-Catalyzed Hairpin Assembly for the On-Site Detection of Salmonella typhimurium in Milk
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a colourimetric assay based on aptamer-catalysed hairpin assembly signal amplification strategy (Y-CHA ) for the detection of S. typhimurium in milk.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a concentration range of 10(2) to 10(6) CFU/mL, with a sensitivity of 2.4 × 10(2) CFU/mL under optimal conditions and 2.8 × 10(3) CFU/mL in real milk samples.

Title: A Colorimetric Strategy Based on Aptamer-Catalyzed Hairpin Assembly for the On-Site Detection of Salmonella typhimurium in Milk
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a colourimetric assay based on aptamer-catalysed hairpin assembly signal amplification strategy (Y-CHA ) for the detection of S. typhimurium in milk.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a concentration range of 10(2) to 10(6) CFU/mL, with a sensitivity of 2.4 × 10(2) CFU/mL under optimal conditions and 2.8 × 10(3) CFU/mL in real milk samples.

Title: Sensitive detection of S. Aureus using aptamer- and vancomycin -copper nanoclusters as dual recognition strategy
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer- and antibiotic-based dual detection sensor, combines copper nanoclusters (CuNCs) for the detection of S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Showed a linear range of 10(2)-10(8) CFU/mL, and a detection limit of 80 CFU/mL after 45 min.

Title: A new electrochemical aptasensor based on gold/nitrogen-doped carbon nano-onions for the detection of Staphylococcus aureus
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an electrochemical aptasensor based on SPEs modified with AuNPs and NCNOs for the detection of S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Measured S. aureus quickly with a limit of detection of 3 CFU/mL in the linear range of 10–10(8) CFU/mL.

Title: Detection of Listeria monocytogenes Using Luminol-Functionalized AuNF-Labeled Aptamer Recognition and Magnetic Separation
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer-linked biofunctional magnetic nanomaterial system for highly sensitive and specific LM detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a linear concentration range 1.0 × 10(1)-1.0 × 10(5) CFU/mL and detect L. monocytogenes at levels as low as 6 CFU/mL in milk samples.

Title: A Low-Field Magnetic Resonance Imaging Aptasensor for the Rapid and Visual Sensing of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in Food, Juice, and Water
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a low-field magnetic resonance imaging (LF-MRI) aptasensor based on the difference in magnetic behaviour of two magnetic nanoparticles with diameters of 10 (MN10) and 400 nm (MN400) for the rapid detection of P. aeruginosa.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Show a detection limit of 100 cfu/mL with a wide linear range from 3.1 × 10(2) to 3.1 × 10(7) cfu/mL.

Title: DNA Aptamer-Conjugated Magnetic Graphene Oxide for Pathogenic Bacteria Aggregation: Selective and Enhanced Photothermal Therapy for Effective and Rapid Killing
Objective/Mechanism: Apt@MGO nanoplatform for selective and rapid eradication of MRSA under NIR laser irradiation.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Apt@MGO resulted in ∼78% MRSA and over >97% MRSA cell inactivation in dispersed and aggregated states, respectively, under 200 seconds of exposure to NIR irradiation (808 nm, 1.1 W cm–2).
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): The aptamer itself did not cause any cell activation when incubated with MRSA cells, and also under no NIR laser illumination.

Title: Enhancement of the peroxidase-like activity of aptamers modified gold nanoclusters by bacteria for colorimetric detection of Salmonella typhimurium
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a colorimetric aptasensor using gold nanoclusters (aptamers@BSA-AuNCs) for the detection of S. typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a wide linear range of 10(1)-10(6) cfu/mL with a detection limit as low as 1 cfu/mL.

Title: Enhancement of the peroxidase-like activity of aptamers modified gold nanoclusters by bacteria for colorimetric detection of Salmonella typhimurium
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a colorimetric aptasensor using gold nanoclusters (aptamers@BSA-AuNCs) for the detection of S. typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a wide linear range of 10(1)-10(6) cfu/mL with a detection limit as low as 1 cfu/mL.

Title: Ratiometric fluorescence resonance energy transfer aptasensor for highly sensitive and selective detection of Acinetobacter baumannii bacteria in urine sample using carbon dots as optical nanoprobes
Objective/Mechanism: Develop an ingenious ratiometric fluorescent aptasensor for the detection of (Ab) bacteria based on FRET between ortho-phenylenediamine carbon dots (o-CD), nitrogen-doped carbon nanodots (NCND), and graphene oxide (GO).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display linear range from 2.0 × 10(3) to 4.5 × 10(7) cfu/mL and the low detection limit of 3.0 × 10(2) cfu/mL.
Stability: After a storage period of 4 weeks, over 90% of the initial response remained of the aptasenosr.

Title: Rapid and sensitive determination of Pseudomonas aeruginosa by using a glassy carbon electrode modified with gold nanoparticles and aptamer-imprinted polydopamine
Objective/Mechanism: Develop an electrochemical sensor based on a combination of aptasensing and molecular imprinting employing GCE/AuNP/Aptamer-MIP for ultrasensitive detection of P. aeruginosa.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a wide linear dynamic concentration range of 10(1) to 10(7) CFU/ml with a low detection limit of 1 CFU/ml.
Stability: The GCE/AuNP/Aptamer-MIP aptasensor signal remained unchanged, and only a 3% decrease in the peak current occurred after 50 repetitive cycles.

Title: Aptasensor for the Detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in Sputum Utilising CFP10-ESAT6 Protein as a Selective Biomarker
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a portable electrochemical aptamer-antibody-based sandwich biosensor via CapApt/GP/PANI-modified SPGE surface for M. tb. detection in clinical sputum samples.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Detection of the CFP10-ESAT6 antigen ranged from 5 to 500 ng/mL, with a detection limit of 1.5 ng/mL.

Title: One-Step Fabrication of Stimuli-Responsive Chitosan-Platinum Brushes for Listeria monocytogenes Detection
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a label-free electrochemical biosensor using a new one-step simultaneous sonoelectrodeposition of platinum and chitosan (CHI/Pt) to create a biomimetic nanostructure for Listeria monocytogenes detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: LOD of the CHI/Pt-aptamer brushes in PBS was 2.5 ± 0.3 CFU/mL, 3.3 ± 0.9 CFU/mL in chicken broth.

Objective/Mechanism: Developed a fluorescence resonance energy transfer polyaptasensor based on an aptamer cocktail/graphene oxide for bacterial detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Detection limit as low as 10 CFU/mL.

Title: An electrochemical aptasensor for Mycobacterium tuberculosis ESAT-6 antigen detection using bimetallic organic framework
Objective/Mechanism: A label-free electrochemical aptasensor was developed using NG@Zr-MOF-on-Ce-MOF@Tb nanohybrid for sensitive detection of ESAT-6.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Displayed a wide linear range from 100 fg/mL to 10 ng/mL with a limit of detection (LOD) of 12 fg/mL.
Stability: The current remained at 95.77% and 88.72% of the initial current after storing at at 4℃ for 8 days and 16 days, respectively.

Title: Microfluidic thread-based electrochemical aptasensor for rapid detection of Vibrio parahaemolyticus
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a thread-based microfluidic nano-aptasensor based on MoS2 modified threaded electrodes for V. parahaemolyticus detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The proposed aptasensor has a dynamic detection range of 10–10(6) CFU/mL, a detection limit of 5.74 CFU/mL, and an assay time of 30 min.

Title: Controllable design of a nano-bio aptasensing interface based on tetrahedral framework nucleic acids in an integrated microfluidic platform
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a tetrahedral framework nucleic acids-based aptasensing interface in the microfluidic system for E. coli O157: H7 detection and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) determination.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: A calibration curve was constructed over 10(1) to 10(5) CFU/mL, with a limit of detection of 10(1) CFU/mL.

Title: A turn-on-type fluorescence resonance energy transfer aptasensor for vibrio detection using aptamer-modified polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane-perovskite quantum dots/Ti3C2 MXenes composite probes
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a turn-on–type aptasensor based on FRET pair using aptamer modified polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane-perovskite quantum dots (POSS-PQDs-Apt) as signal probe and titanium carbide (Ti3C2) MXenes as quencher for Vibrio parahaemolyticus (VP) determination.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Under optimized conditions, the assay can determine VP in the concentration range 10(2) - 10(6) cfu/mL with the detection limit (LOD) of 30 cfu/mL and 100 cfu/mL by naked eye in aquaculture water.

Title: Ultra-sensitive photoelectrochemical aptamer biosensor for detecting E. coli O157:H7 based on nonmetallic plasmonic two-dimensional hydrated defective tungsten oxide nanosheets coupling with nitrogen-doped graphene quantum dots (dWO3•H2O@N-GQDs)
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a novel PEC aptasensor based on dWO3•H2O@N-GQDs for ultrasensitive detection of E. coli O157:H7.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a limit of detection of 0.05 CFU/mL and a wide linear detection range from 0.1 to 10(4) CFU/mL.

Title: Electrochemical aptasensor for simultaneous detection of foodborne pathogens based on a double stirring bars-assisted signal amplification strategy
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a double stirring bar-based signal-amplified strategy using aptamer-embedded tetrahedral DNA nanostructures for the simultaneous electrochemical detection of Vibrio parahaemolyticus (V.P) and Salmonella typhimurium (S.T).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a lower detection limit of 4 CFU/mL for V.P. within a detection range of 10–10(8) CFU/mL.

Title: Electrochemical aptasensor for simultaneous detection of foodborne pathogens based on a double stirring bars-assisted signal amplification strategy
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a double stirring bar-based signal-amplified strategy using aptamer-embedded tetrahedral DNA nanostructures for the simultaneous electrochemical detection of Vibrio parahaemolyticus (V.P) and Salmonella typhimurium (S.T).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a lower detection limit of 7 CFU/mL for S.T. within a detection range of 10–10(8) CFU/mL.

Title: Hollow carbon nanocapsules-based nitrogen-doped carbon nanofibers with rosary-like structure as a high surface substrate for impedimetric detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an electrochemical aptasensor based on hollow carbon nanocapsule-based nitrogen-doped carbon nanofibers (CNCNF) with a rosary-like structure for the detection of PA.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The linear range and LOD of the aptasensor were 101-107 CFU/ml and 1 CFU/ml.
Stability: After 8 days of storage in Fe(CN)6 3-/4- at 4°C, the electrode was found to be 89% of its initial activity.

Title: A novel photoelectrochemical aptamer sensor based on rare-earth doped Bi2WO6 and Ag2S for the rapid detection of Vibrio parahaemolyticus
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a novel photoelectrochemical aptasensor based on rare-earth doped Bi2WO6 and Ag2S for the detection of V. parahaemolyticus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Showed a wide linear range from 3.2 × 10(2) CFU/mL to 3.2 × 10(8) CFU/mL, and a detection limit of 40 CFU/mL.
Stability: After 2 weeks of storage at 4°C in a refrigerator, the biosensor retained 95% of its initial response.

Title: A Novel Photoelectrochemical Aptamer Sensor Based on CdTe Quantum Dots Enhancement and Exonuclease I-Assisted Signal Amplification for Listeria monocytogenes Detection
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a photoelectrochemical aptasensor based on WO3, CdTe QDs, and Exo I auxiliary signal amplification for the detection of L. monocytogenes.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Showed a detection limit of 45 CFU/mL over the concentration range of 1.3 × 10(1) - 1.3 × 10 (7) CFU/mL.

Title: A novel smartphone-based colorimetric aptasensor for on-site detection of Escherichia coli O157:H7 in milk
Objective/Mechanism: A colorimetric aptasensor was developed using GNP-Apt coupling with an MWCNT@CIP probe for detecting E. coli O157:H7 in milk.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a concentration of 8.43 × 10(3) cfu/mL in pure culture, and 5.24 × 10(2) cfu/mL in artificially contaminated milk after 1h.

Title: Colorimetric determination of Listeria monocytogenes using aptamer and urease dual-labeled magnetic nanoparticles and cucurbit[7]uril-mediated supramolecular assembly of gold nanoparticle
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a colorimetric strategy using apt-MNP-urease conjugate for the detection of L. monocytogenes.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a concentration range from 10 to 10(6) cfu/mL, and the visual determination can be done down to 10 cfu/mL.

Title: One-step colorimetric detection of Staphylococcus aureus based on target-induced shielding against the peroxidase mimicking activity of aptamer-functionalized gold-coated iron oxide nanocomposites
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a colorimetric sensor using apt-Fe3O4/Au nanocomposites for the detection of Staphylococcus aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a linear range from 10 to 10(6) CFU/mL, with the visible limit of detection as low as 10 CFU/mL.

Title: Sensitive colorimetric aptasensor based on g-C3N4@Cu2O composites for detection of Salmonella typhimurium in food and water
Objective/Mechanism: A colorimetric aptasensor using graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) nanosheets and copper oxide(I) (Cu2O) nanocrystals was developed for detecting S. typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited linear range from 1.5 × 10(1) to 1.5 × 10(5) CFU/ml, with a detection limit of 15 CFU/ml.

Title: An efficient SERS platform for the ultrasensitive detection of Staphylococcus aureus and Listeria monocytogenes via wheat germ agglutinin-modified magnetic SERS substrate and streptavidin/aptamer co-functionalized SERS tags
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptasensor using WGA modified-Fe3O4@Au MNPs and Streptavidin (SA)/aptamer co-functionalized SERS tags for S. aureus and L. mono detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The LOD for S. aureus was 3 cells/mL and a favorable linear relation (10-10(7) cells/mL).

Title: An efficient SERS platform for the ultrasensitive detection of Staphylococcus aureus and Listeria monocytogenes via wheat germ agglutinin-modified magnetic SERS substrate and streptavidin/aptamer co-functionalized SERS tags
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptasensor using WGA modified-Fe3O4@Au MNPs and Streptavidin (SA)/aptamer co-functionalized SERS tags for S. aureus and L. mono detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The LOD for L. mono was 5 cells/mL and a favorable linear relation (10-10(7) cells/mL).

Title: A universal SERS-label immunoassay for pathogen bacteria detection based on Fe3O4@Au-aptamer separation and antibody-protein A orientation recognition
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a SERS aptasensor using aptamer-conjugated Fe3O4@Au magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) and PA modified-SERS tags (Au@DTNB@PA) for the detection of bacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The limit of detection (LOD) was 10 cells/mL for E. coli.

Title: A universal SERS-label immunoassay for pathogen bacteria detection based on Fe3O4@Au-aptamer separation and antibody-protein A orientation recognition
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a SERS aptasensor using aptamer-conjugated Fe3O4@Au magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) and PA modified-SERS tags (Au@DTNB@PA) for the detection of bacteria.

Objective/Mechanism: Developed a SERS aptasensor using aptamer-conjugated Fe3O4@Au magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) and PA modified-SERS tags (Au@DTNB@PA) for the detection of bacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The limit of detection (LOD) for S. typhi was 25 cells/mL.

Title: Fabrication of gold/silver nanodimer SERS probes for the simultaneous detection of Salmonella typhimurium and Staphylococcus aureus
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer-facilitated gold/silver nanodimer SERS probe for the simultaneous detection of the two bacteria with the help of magnetic separation enrichment.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a linear range of 10(2) to 10(7) cfu/mL, with a detection limit of 50 cfu/mL.

Title: Fabrication of gold/silver nanodimer SERS probes for the simultaneous detection of Salmonella typhimurium and Staphylococcus aureus
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer-facilitated gold/silver nanodimer SERS probe for the simultaneous detection of the two bacteria with the help of magnetic separation enrichment.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a linear range of 3.2 × 10(2) to 3.2 × 10(7) cfu/mL, with a detection limit of 96 cfu/mL.

Title: Electrochemical Biosensing Interface Based on Carbon Dots-Fe3O4 Nanomaterial for the Determination of Escherichia coli O157:H7
Objective/Mechanism: A carbon dots-Fe3O4 nanomaterial (CDs-Fe3O4)-based electrochemical aptasensor for E. coli O157:H7 detection was developed.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited the detection range of 10–10(8) CFU/ml, and the detection limit of 6.88 CFU/ml.

Title: Upconversion Nanoprobes Based on a Horseradish Peroxidase-Regulated Dual-Mode Strategy for the Ultrasensitive Detection of Staphylococcus aureus in Meat
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a colorimetric and fluorescent dual-mode nanoprobe using apt-MNPs and HRP-UCNPs-cDNA for the detection of S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Obtained limits of detection of 22 CFU/mL for fluorescence and 20 CFU/mL for colorimetry in a linear range of 56–5.6 × 10(6) CFU/mL.

Title: Rapid and sensitive detection of Escherichia coli O157:H7 based on silver nanocluster fluorescent probe
Objective/Mechanism: Detection of E. coli O157:H7 in food based on aptamer-modified silver nanocluster fluorescent probes.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The linear range was 10–10(6) CFU/mL, and the detection limit was 0.2549 CFU/mL in the buffer and 0.6031 CFU/mL in the milk simulation sample.

Title: Novel Competitive Voltammetric Aptasensor Based on Electrospun Carbon Nanofibers-Gold Nanoparticles Modified Graphite Electrode for Salmonella enterica serovar Detection
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an electrochemical aptasensor based on aptamer-linked GNPs/CNF-Chi/GEs for the detection of Salmonella enterica Serovar.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a linear range of 10 to 10(5) CFU/mL with the limit of detection (LOD) 1.223 CFU/mL.

Objective/Mechanism: Identify an aptamer against E.coli and develop a detection platform using gold nanoparticles and graphene oxide with aptamer conjugation.

Title: Selection and Identification of a DNA Aptamer for Multidrug-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Using an In-House Cell-SELEX Methodology
Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers against MDR A. baumannii.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Preferential binding to A. baumannii over other species. 25% of positive events for A. baumannii above the 12.66% of the negative control.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): Aptamer binding does not seem to interfere with the A. baumannii cell growth even after 24h (5.88E+02 x 1.45E+03; p=0.700).

Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers that inhibit the biofilm formation of the S. suis target strain.

Title: Aptamer-Targeted Drug Delivery for Staphylococcus aureus Biofilm
Objective/Mechanism: Aptamer-targeted liposomes encapsulating antibiotics for accumulation and delivery to eradicate S. aureus biofilm.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: SA31-modified liposomes fully eradicated all viable, culturable bacteria in all biofilm samples.
Stability: SA23 appeared more stable than the other aptamers in plasma over a 16-hour incubation period.

Title: Targeted inhibition of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus biofilm formation by a graphene oxide-loaded aptamer/berberine bifunctional complex
Objective/Mechanism: Identify a PBP2a-targeted aptamer in conjunction with GO for the delivery of berberine to treat chronic infections caused by MRSA biofilms.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The linear range was 10^3–10^7 CFU/mL, and the detection limit for the fluorescent assay was 800 CFU/mL. The inhibition rate peaked at 92.8% after treatment with the GO-berberine/aptamer 1 (containing 200 nM aptamer 1) complex.

Title: Targeted inhibition of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus biofilm formation by a graphene oxide-loaded aptamer/berberine bifunctional complex
Objective/Mechanism: Identify a PBP2a-targeted aptamer in conjunction with GO for the delivery of berberine to treat chronic infections caused by MRSA biofilms.

Title: Investigating the anti-streptococcal biofilm effect of ssDNA aptamer-silver nanoparticles complex on a titanium-based substrate
Objective/Mechanism: Silver nanoparticles-aptamer complex (AptBH-AgNPs) that binds to the surface receptors of streptococcal strains and inhibits biofilm formation.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: AptBH-AgNPs at a concentration of 100 μg/mL after 48 h inhibited 43% of the biofilm formation and degraded 63% of the formed biofilm.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): AgNPs-AptBH is weakly toxic, with cell viability of 96% even at 100 μg/mL. At 75 and 100 μg/mL, these concentrations caused ∼approximately 9% and 11% hemolysis, respectively.
Stability: AgNPs-AptBH complex has not decomposed over time for 360 min in the cell culture medium.

Title: DNA-aptamer-nanographene oxide as a targeted bio-theragnostic system in antimicrobial photodynamic therapy against Porphyromonas gingivalis
Objective/Mechanism: DNA-aptamer-NGO, a targeted bio-theragnostic system against P. gingivalis for antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: MIC of DNA-aptamer-NGO was 62.5 nM, and MBC was 125 nM. aPDT using 1/2 × and 1/4 × MBC of DNA-aptamer-NGO plus irradiation of the diode laser light (1 min) has a significantly anti-biofilm effect; percentage of apoptosis cells treated with DNA-aptamer-NGO at 1/2 × and 1/4 × MIC plus diode laser were 13.9% and 12.7%; and 1/2 × MIC of DNA-aptamer-NGO, resulted in 40.3% inactivation of metabolic activity compared to 1/4 × MBC of DNA-aptamer-NGO, where only 22.2% inactivation.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): At high concentrations of DNA-aptamer-NGO, incubated for 24 hours with human red blood cells, the percentage did not exceed 5%. Also, at different concentrations, the mean percentage of HGF cell viability ranges from 95.2% to 87.6%.

Title: Electrochemical Aptasensor for the Detection of the Key Virulence Factor YadA of Yersinia enterocolitica
Objective/Mechanism: Identify an aptamer against YadA and develop an electrochemical biosensor for its detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a linear range between 7.0 × 10(4) and 7.0 × 10(7) CFU/mL, and the limit of detection of SWV was 7.0 × 10(4) CFU/mL.

Title: Application of G-quadruplex aptamer conjugated MSNs to deliver ampicillin for suppressing S. aureus biofilm on mice bone
Objective/Mechanism: MSNs-APT-AMP nanosystem for antibiofilm activity against S. aureus biofilm.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: No significant biofilm on the surface of the bone after 48 h treatment with 100 µg/mL of the three-component system.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): No significant toxicity at 100 µg/mL for MCF-7 cells in 48 h.

Title: Novel nanozyme-catalyzed and magnetically assisted colorimetric biosensor for Staphylococcus aureus detection with a low matrix effect from complex environments
Objective/Mechanism: Vancomycin-modified magnetic nanoparticles (Fe3O4 @Au-Van MNPs) combined with an aptamer were prepared for S. aureus detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The biosensor can distinguish more than 100 CFU/mL of pathogens by the naked eye and LOD of 2 CFU/mL for S. aureus.

Objective/Mechanism: Develop SERS-based aptasensor to detect OspA in serum samples.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: OspA limit-of-detection determined to be 1 × 10−4 ng/mL with 91% sensitivity and 96% specificity.

Title: A surface-enhanced Raman scattering aptasensor for Escherichia coli detection based on high-performance 3D substrate and hot spot effect
Objective/Mechanism: Developed SERS aptasensor composed of Apt-AgNPs-CS gel and GNS@4-MBA-Apt NPs for detection of E. coli in food.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a detection limit of 3.46 CFU/mL with a wide dynamic linear range from 3.2 × 10(1) to 3.2 × 10(7) CFU/mL and a good recovery rate (>90%).

Title: Zirconium-Based Metal–Organic Framework and Ti3C2Tx Nanosheet-Based Faraday Cage-Type Electrochemical Aptasensor for Escherichia coli Detection
Objective/Mechanism: A Faraday-cage-type electrochemical aptasensor based on Zr-Fc MOF/AuNPs/4-MPBA framework was developed for the detection of E. coli O157:H7.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a detection limit of 3 CFU/mL and a linear range of 10-1.0 × 10(5) CFU/mL.
Stability: 95.6% of the initial current of the aptasensor was reserved when stored for 14 days at 4°C.

Title: An innovative dual recognition aptasensor for specific detection of Staphylococcus aureus based on Au/Fe3O4 binary hybrid
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an imprinted aptasensor (apt-AuNPs@ Fe3O4) for the quantification of S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a wide linear range of 10(1)-10(7) CFU/mL with a Limit of Detection (LOD ) of 1 CFU/mL.
Stability: The aptasensor retained approximately 95% of its original activity for four weeks.

Title: An ultrasensitive sandwich-type electrochemical aptasensor using silver nanoparticle/titanium carbide nanocomposites for the determination of Staphylococcus aureus in milk
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a novel sandwich-type electrochemical aptasensor using AgNPs@Ti3C2 nanocomposites for the detection of S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Showed a low detection limit (LOD) of 1 CFU/mL and a linear range of 52–5.2 × 10(7) CFU/mL.
Stability: 92.68% of the initial current of the aptasensor was reserved when stored for 15 days at 4°C.

Title: An ultrasensitive and dual-recognition SERS biosensor based on Fe3O4@Au-Teicoplanin and aptamer functionalized Au@Ag nanoparticles for detection of Staphylococcus aureus
Objective/Mechanism: The SERS biosensor based on Fe3O4@Au-Tcp NPs as a capture probe and Au@Ag-DTNB-Apt NPs as a signal probe for the detection of S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Showed detection limit of 1.09 CFU/mL with a broad dynamic linear range of 7.6 × 10(1)-7.6 × 10(7) CFU/mL within 50 min.

Title: Paper-Based Electrodes Conjugated with Tungsten Disulfide Nanostructure and Aptamer for Impedimetric Detection of Listeria monocytogenes
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptasensor based on ePAD that employs a tungsten disulfide (WS2)/aptamer hybrid for the detection of L. monocytogenes.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The limit of detection (LoD) was 10 CFU/mL, with a linear range of 10(1)-10(8) CFU/mL.
Stability: Aptasensor gives a stable impedance response over a period of 15 days.

Title: Sandwich fluorometric method for dual-role recognition of Listeria monocytogenes based on antibiotic-affinity strategy and fluorescence quenching effect
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a sandwich fluorimetric method (MNPs-Van) for dual-role recognition of L. monocytogenes.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a low detection limit (LOD) of 2.8 × 10(2) CFU/mL in 1.5 h with a concentration range over 10(2)-2 × 10(8) CFU/mL.

Title: Dual recognition and highly sensitive detection of Listeria monocytogenes in food by fluorescence enhancement effect based on Fe3O4@ZIF-8-aptamer
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a fluorescence enhancement effect-based detection strategy based on Fe3O4@ZIF-8@aptamer for L. monocytogenes.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The linear range for detection of pure culture was 1.4 × 10(1) to 1.4 × 10(7) CFU/mL, with a detection limit of 0.88 CFU/mL in about 70 min.

Title: Colorimetric detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa by aptamer-functionalized gold nanoparticles
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a colorimetric biosensor using aptamer-functionalized AuNPs for identifying P. aeruginosa.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: P. aeruginosa was detected after 5 h for concentrations from 10(8) to 10(5) CFU/mL, with 10(5) and 10(4) CFU/mL being the detection limits for colour change by the naked eye and UV-Vis spectrometry, respectively.

Title: Label-Free Electrochemical Aptasensor for the Detection of the 3-O-C12-HSL Quorum-Sensing Molecule in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Objective/Mechanism: An electrochemical aptasensor using a carbon-based SPE modified with AuNPs was developed for the detection of 3-O-C12-HSL.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a logarithmic range from 0.5 to 30 µM, with a limit of detection of 145 ng mL−1 (0.5 µM).

Target Organism: Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) BPA-12 and Escherichia Coli (E. Coli) EPEC 4
Objective/Mechanism: Determine the antibiofilm activity and binding specificity of the polyclonal DNA aptamers on S. aureus BPA-12 and E. coli EPEC 4.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Showed the percentage of antibiofilm activity against S. aureus BPA-12 (25.8%) and E. coli EPEC 4 (0.3%).

Objective/Mechanism: Identify an aptamer against DevR and inhibit DevR-dependent transcription by blocking DevR dimerisation and DNA-binding activity in Mycobacterium smegmatis.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: APT-1, APT-2, APT-5, and APT-7 exhibited a maximum of ∼40% inhibition of Rv1738 promoter activity.

Objective/Mechanism: By targeting DevR dimerization, it blocks the essential step in DevR activation, thus intercepting dormancy pathways in mycobacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: APT-1, APT-2, APT-5, and APT-7 exhibited a maximum of ∼40% inhibition of Rv1738 promoter activity.

Outcome/Inhibitory effect: APT-4 inhibited Rv1738 promoter activity in a time-dependent manner, with an inhibition value of 61% at 96 hours and inhibited DevR–DevR interaction in vivo by ∼35%.

Title: Targeted mesoporous silica nanoparticles for improved inhibition of disinfectant resistant Listeria monocytogenes and lower environmental pollution
Objective/Mechanism: BAC-encapsulated, aptamer-functionalized silica nanoparticles (AptBACNP) effectively killed only the target bacterium, L. monocytogenes, at lower doses, but not other bacteria.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Inhibition (MIC value) of BAC resistant Listeria strains with 8 times less the usual disinfectant dose.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): MSNPs are slightly cytotoxic to erythrocytes and MCF-7 cells at concentrations more than 25 µg/ml.

Title: Aptamer decorated emodin nanoparticles-assisted delivery of dermcidin-derived peptide DCD-1L: Photoactive bio-theragnostic agent for Enterococcus faecalis biofilm destruction
Objective/Mechanism: Apt@EmoNp-DCD-1L that binds E. faecalis, enabling targeted delivery of emodin nanoparticles and DCD-1L for anti-biofilm activity.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: aPDT using Apt@EmoNp-DCD-1L caused ≈99.99% reduction of E. faecalis viability and strong biofilm disruption at sub-MIC concentrations (7.8 and 15.6 µM).

Title: SELEX against whole-cell bacteria resulted in lipopolysaccharide binding aptamers
Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers that bind to LPS on Gram-negative bacteria and inhibit the LPS-induced inflammatory response, thereby inhibiting bacterial infections.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: When aptamers bind to the LPS, the macrophage polarization ability of LPS can decrease, and the secreted nitrite level diminishes.

Title: Simultaneous Amperometric Aptasensor Based on Diazonium Grafted Screen-Printed Carbon Electrode for Detection of CFP10 and MPT64 Biomarkers for Early Tuberculosis Diagnosis
Objective/Mechanism: Amperometric dual aptasensor for the simultaneous detection of M. tb. secreted antigens CFP10 and MPT64 for the diagnosis of TB.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a detection limit of 1.82 ng/mL and a linear range of 0.75–250 ng/mL for MPT64 antigen within 2.5 h.

Title: Simultaneous Amperometric Aptasensor Based on Diazonium Grafted Screen-Printed Carbon Electrode for Detection of CFP10 and MPT64 Biomarkers for Early Tuberculosis Diagnosis
Objective/Mechanism: Amperometric dual aptasensor for the simultaneous detection of M. tb. secreted antigens CFP10 and MPT64 for the diagnosis of TB.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a detection limit of 1.68 ng/mL and a linear range of 0.5–100 ng/mL for CFP10 antigen within 2.5 h.

Title: Aptamer-Based Fluorescence Detection and Selective Disinfection of Salmonella Typhimurium by Using Hollow Carbon Nitride Nanosphere
Objective/Mechanism: Develop an off-on fluorescence aptasensor for the detection of S. typhimurium and use HCNS-Cap for disinfection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The fluorescence assay showed a linear range of 30 to 3 × 10(4) CFU/mL and a detection limit of 13 CFU/mL. The bactericidal efficiency of HCNS-Cap (95.0%) within 12 h was better than that of HCNS (85.1%) and Cap (72.9%).

Title: Aptamer-AuNP-conjugated carboxymethyl chitosan-functionalized graphene oxide for colorimetric identification of Salmonella typhimurium
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a novel aptamer-AuNP-conjugated carboxymethyl chitosan–functionalized graphene oxide (CMC/GO@Apt-Au NP) probe for the determination of S. typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a linear range from 10(2) to 10(7) CFU/mL with a limit of detection (LOD) of 10 CFU/mL.
Stability: The relative response of aptasensor decreased to ~ 77% within 11 days of storage.

Title: Electrochemical biosensor for detecting pathogenic bacteria based on a hybridization chain reaction and CRISPR-Cas12a
Objective/Mechanism: An electrochemical biosensor platform based on HCR-based CRISPR-Cas12a for specific detection of S. typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Selectively and sensitively quantify S. typhimurium in samples with detection limits of 20 CFU/mL and a linear range of 10-10(8) CFU/mL.

Title: Multiple amplification-based fluorometric aptasensor for highly sensitive detection of Staphylococcus aureus
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a fluorometric aptasensor for the detection of S. aureus using magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The proposed fluorometric aptasensor displays LOD of (1.23 cfu/mL, a wide linear range (1 ~ 10(8) cfu/mL), and a fast detection speed (~ 1.5 h).

Title: Potentiometric aptasensing of Escherichia coli based on electrogenerated chemiluminescence as a highly sensitive readout
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a potentiometric aptasensor by electrogenerated chemiluminescence (ECL) using SWCNTs-aptamer modified electrode to detect E. coli.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Shows a highly sensitive response to E. coli O157: H7 in the linear range of 5-1000 CFU/mL with a low detection limit of 2 CFU/mL.

Title: Surface plasmon resonance aptasensor for Brucella detection in milk
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a surface plasmon resonance (SPR) aptasensor for the detection of B. melitensis in milk samples.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: LOD value as low as 27 ± 11 cells.

Title: Surface plasmon resonance aptasensor for Brucella detection in milk
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a surface plasmon resonance (SPR) aptasensor for the detection of B. melitensis in milk samples.

Title: Surface plasmon resonance aptasensor for Brucella detection in milk
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a surface plasmon resonance (SPR) aptasensor for the detection of B. melitensis in milk samples.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: B70 showed about 35% higher affinity for Brucella cells than the B46 aptamer, and the SPR sensor showed an LOD of 27 ± 11 cells.

Title: Surface plasmon resonance aptasensor for Brucella detection in milk

Title: Detection of E. coli Bacteria in Milk by an Acoustic Wave Aptasensor with an Anti-Fouling Coating
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an electromagnetic piezoelectric acoustic sensor device (EMPAS) based on SiO2-MEG-NH2-Aptamer for the detection of E.coli. in milk samples.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Selective measurement of E. coli in PBS and in cow’s milk samples down to limits of detection of 35 and 8 CFU/mL, respectively, with a linear range of 10–10(7) CFU/mL.

Title: A new cognate aptamer pair-based sandwich-type electrochemical biosensor for sensitive detection of Staphylococcus aureus
Objective/Mechanism: A sandwich-type signal-on electrochemical aptasensor using a cognate aptamer pair was developed for the detection of S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a limit of detection (LOD) of 39 CFUs and 414 CFUs in buffer and spiked tap water samples, respectively, with the cognate pair of SA37@Cy5 and SA81@FAM.

Title: Introducing an SPRi-based titration assay using aptamers for the detection of Legionella pneumophila
Objective/Mechanism: SPRi-based titration assay using Lp aptamer for detecting L. pneumophila.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The limit of detection for this system was 10(4.4) cells/ml, with a linear dynamic range of 10(4.3) –10(7.7) cells/ml.

Title: Naked-eye detection of Staphylococcus aureus in powdered milk and infant formula using gold nanoparticles
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a colorimetric LSPR aptasensor using gold nanoparticles for the detection of S. aureus in milk and infant formula.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Could be visually detected within 30 min, with detection limits of 7.5 × 10(4) CFU/mL and 8.4 × 10(4) CFU/mL in milk and infant formula, respectively.

Title: Rapid and selective detection of Bacillus cereus in food using cDNA-based up-conversion fluorescence spectrum copy and aptamer modified magnetic separation
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptansensor for Bacillus cereus detection based on up-conversion and magnetic nanomaterials (UCNPs-cDNA-Apt-MNPs complex).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a linear range of 49-49 × 10(6) cfu/mL under the optimal conditions with a detection limit of 22 cfu/mL.

Title: Dual-mode sensor based on the synergy of magnetic separation and functionalized probes for the ultrasensitive detection of Clostridium perfringens
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a dual-mode aptasensor using the synergy between fluorescent and electrochemical signals based on a DNA walker and hybridization chain reaction (HCR) for Clostridium perfringens detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Displayed an excellent analytical performance for C. perfringens at a concentration of 1 to 10(8) CFU/g and a minimum concentration of 1 CFU/g in real samples.

Title: Aptamer-based colorimetric detection of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus by using a CRISPR/Cas12a system and recombinase polymerase amplification
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer-based colorimetry sensor using a CRISPR/Cas12a system and recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) for sensitive detection of MRSA.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: MRSA was detected as low as 8 CFU/mL and can be quantified with a linear range of 10 CFU/mL to 10(5) CFU/mL.

Title: DNAzyme-controlled plasmonic coupling for SERS-based determination of Salmonella typhimurium using hybridization chain reaction self-assembled G-quadruplex
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a SERS aptasensor based on hybridization chain reaction (HCR) self-assembled G-quadruplex DNAzyme (GQH DNAzyme)-controlled plasmonic coupling for S. typhimurium detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a linear range from 5 to 5.0 × 10(5) cfu/mL and the limit of detection (LOD) of 4 cfu/mL.

Title: A dual-mode aptasensor for foodborne pathogens detection using Pt, phenylboric acid and ferrocene modified Ti3C2 MXenes nanoprobe
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a dual-mode aptasensor based on electrochemical and colorimetric modes using PBA-Fc@Pt@MXenes nanoprobe for the detection of V.P in shrimps.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Showed a LOD and linear range of 5 CFU/mL and 10(1) to 10 (8) CFU/mL by electrochemical mode and 30 CFU/mL and 10(2) to 10 (8) CFU/mL by coulometric mode.
Stability: The electrochemical signal retained 89.6% of its original value after 2 weeks.

Title: Aptamer-conjugated magnetic Fe3O4@Au core-shell multifunctional nanoprobe: A three-in-one aptasensor for selective capture, sensitive SERS detection and efficient near-infrared light triggered photothermal therapy of Staphylococcus aureus
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptasensor based on Fe3O4@Au nanocomposites (NCs) for capture, SERS detection, and photothermal therapy (PTT) of S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The detection limit is 25 cfu/mL, the cell capture efficiency (CCE) is as high as 68% and it has a high photothermal conversion efficiency of 39.28%.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): The cytotoxicity of Fe3O4@Au-Apt NCs to S. aureus is negligible.
Stability: The SERS intensity of S. aureus on the Fe3O4@Au-Apt NCs remains almost unchanged within 12 days.

Title: Alpha-Gal Bound Aptamer and Vancomycin Synergistically Reduce Staphylococcus aureus Infection In Vivo
Objective/Mechanism: αSA31 rescue α-1, 3-galactosyltransferase (−/−) knockout (GTKO) mice from induced MRSA sepsis.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: 3.5-fold more (p < 0.05) pretreated MRSA were phagocytized when also treated with αSA31 and 7/12 mice treated with vancomycin plus αSA31 survived in-vivo.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): No toxicity was observed, even at 10,000 µg/kg/day.
Stability: αSA31NH2 was significantly more stable (p < 0.01) in human serum, as no degradation was observed after 24 h at 37°C.

Title: Dual-mode sensing platform based on aptamer-tunable catalytic activity of mesoporous polydopamine/MnO2 nanozymes for detecting S. aureus
Objective/Mechanism: Colourimetric-electrochemical sensing platform to detect S. aureus based on a dual-modal strategy.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Shows a low detection limit in 3 CFU/mL with a linear range between 5 and 10(7) CFU/mL and in a real sample with the recovery of 95.15%− 115.28%.

Title: Selecting antibacterial aptamers against the BamA protein in Pseudomonas aeruginosa by incorporating genetic algorithm to optimise computational screening method
Target: Outer membrane protein BamA (β-barrel assembly machinery A)
Objective/Mechanism: Selecting antibacterial aptamers against the BamA protein in Pseudomonas aeruginosa by incorporating a genetic algorithm to optimise the computational screening method.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Treatment of P. aeruginosa with 10 µM Apt31 for 2 h resulted in a significant reduction in CFU/mL and growth percentage.

Title: A point-of-care aptasensor based on the upconversion nanoparticles/MoS2 FRET system for the detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection
Objective/Mechanism: Develop an aptasensor based on FRET between UCNPs-apt/MoS2 for rapid detection of P. aeruginosa.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibit a wide linear detection range 8.7 × 10 ~ 8.7 × 10(7) cfu/mL, and a low limit of detection (LOD) of 15.5 cfu/mL within 1.5 h.

Title: MoS2 nanosheets based label-free colorimetric aptasensor for Escherichia coli O157: H7 detection
Objective/Mechanism: Developed colorimetric aptasensor based on aptamer-functionalized MoS2 nanosheets for the detection of E. coli O157: H7.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Detection of E. coli O157: H7 with a Limit of detection (LOD) of 116 CFU/mL and a linear concentration range of 500–5000 CFU/mL.

Title: An ultrasensitive aptamer-based fluorescent on/off system for trace amount evaluation of Yersinia enterocolitica in food samples
Objective/Mechanism: Fluorescence-based aptasensor using graphene oxide (GO) as a quenching platform was developed for the detection of Y. enterocolitica.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a wide linear response in the concentration range 10 to 1.0 × 10(9) CFU/mL and the limit of detection (LOD) was 3 CFU/mL.
Stability: FAM-aptamer-GO shows better stability in acidic environments, and pH 7 showed the greatest increase. It shows no obvious changes in fluorescence intensity within 60 days.

Title: Aptamer and DNAzyme-Functionalized Cu-MOF Hybrid Nanozymes for the Monitoring and Management of Bacteria-Infected Wounds
Objective/Mechanism: G-quadruplex/hemin DNAzyme-aptamer probes and tannic acid-chelated Au nanoparticle (Au-TA)-decorated Cu-based MOF nanosheets (termed GATC) with triple-enzyme activities were developed for visual detection and efficient antibacterial therapy.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: ~99.7% MRSA inactivation at 3 μg/mL, with simultaneous colorimetric monitoring of infection.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): At 50 μg/mL GATC, the cells showed high viability (>90%), indicating negligible cytotoxicity and good cytocompatibility. The hemolysis rate of the GATC nanozyme was low (<5%).

Title: High-throughput, highly sensitive and rapid SERS detection of Escherichia coli O157:H7 using aptamer-modified Au@macroporous silica magnetic photonic microsphere array
Objective/Mechanism: An aptamer-Au@MMSPM SERS array biochip method was developed for the detection of E. coli O157:H7.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Gave a wide linear detection range (10–10(6) CFU/mL) and low limit of detection (2.20 CFU/mL) for E. coli O157:H7.

Title: Colorimetric aptasensor for detection of Bacillus cytotoxicus spores in milk and ready-to-use food
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a colorimetric assay employing AuNPs and magnetic particles (MPs) for the detection of Bacillus cytotoxicus spores in food.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieving the naked-eye limit of detection as low as 10(2) cfu/mL in water and milk, and 10(4) cfu/mL in mashed potatoes.

Title: An ultrasensitive electrochemical aptasensor using Tyramide-assisted enzyme multiplication for the detection of Staphylococcus aureus
Objective/Mechanism: An electrochemical aptasensor based on the tyramide signal amplification (TSA) technology was developed for the detection of S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a limit of detection (LOD) of 3 CFU/mL in buffer and 8 CFU/mL in both tap water and beef broth.

Title: Applicability of a Green Nanocomposite Consisted of Spongin Decorated Cu2WO4(OH)2 and AgNPs as a High-Performance Aptasensing Platform in Staphylococcus aureus Detection
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptasensing Platform based on a Green Nanocomposite consisting of Spongin Decorated Cu2WO4(OH)2 and AgNPs for Staphylococcus aureus detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Measured S. aureus under a linear concentration range of 10–10(8) CFU/mL and a limit of quantification and detection of 12 and 1 CFU/mL, respectively.

Title: FRET-Based Single-Molecule Detection of Pathogen Protein IsdA Using Computationally Selected Aptamers
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a FRET-based aptasensor for single-molecule detection of IsdA.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: LOD value of T1-280 RNA was 113 pM.
Modification: 5'-Cyanine3 (Cy3) Labeled or 5'-Biotinylated and 5′ end by six nucleotides (ACT GTC), rX = RNA nucleotide

Title: FRET-Based Single-Molecule Detection of Pathogen Protein IsdA Using Computationally Selected Aptamers

Outcome/Inhibitory effect: LOD value of T2-139040 RNA was 17 pM.

Title: Ultrasensitive dual-enhanced sandwich strategy for simultaneous detection of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus based on optimized aptamers-functionalized magnetic capture probes and graphene oxide-Au nanostars SERS tags
Objective/Mechanism: A SERS platform using aptamers modified-Fe3O4@SiO2-Au NCs was developed for simultaneous detection of E. coli and S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The detection limit for E. coli was as low as 10 cfu/mL, and the linear concentration ranged from 10(1)-10(8) cfu/mL.

Title: Ultrasensitive dual-enhanced sandwich strategy for simultaneous detection of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus based on optimized aptamers-functionalized magnetic capture probes and graphene oxide-Au nanostars SERS tags
Objective/Mechanism: A SERS platform using aptamers modified-Fe3O4@SiO2-Au NCs was developed for simultaneous detection of E. coli and S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The detection limit for S. aureus was as low as 10 cfu/mL, and the linear concentration ranged from 10(1)-10(8) cfu/mL.

Title: A novel Aptamer-induced CHA amplification strategy for ultrasensitive detection of Staphylococcus aureus and NIR-triggered photothermal bactericidal Activity based on aptamer-modified magnetic Fe3O4@AuNRs
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a Fe3O4 @AuNRs-aptasensor based on CHA for ultrasensitive detection of S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a linear response ranging from 10(2) to 10(6) CFU/mL and a detection limit of 10(1) CFU/mL under optimal conditions.

Title: Rapid detection of pathogenic bacteria based on a universal dual-recognition FRET sensing system constructed with aptamer-quantum dots and lectin-gold nanoparticles
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a dual-recognition-based sandwich FRET sensor using Aptamer-QDs and Con A-AuNPs for the detection of E. coli.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a linear detection range from 10(2) cfu/mL to 2 × 10(8) cfu/mL with the detection limit of 45 cfu/mL for E. coli, and LOD in the milk and orange juice was 300 cfu/mL and 200 cfu/mL, respectively.

Title: Dual recognition strategy for the rapid and precise detection of Bacillus cereus using post-modified nano-MOF and aptamer
Objective/Mechanism: A dual-recognition strategy using a fluorescent probe, FcMBL-coated nano-MIL-53(Al)-NH2, for detecting B. cereus was developed.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Shows a linear range of 20–2 × 10(8) CFU/mL with a limit of detection of 4 CFU/mL within 60 min.

Title: A SERS bioassay based on vancomycin-modified PEI-interlayered nanocomposite and aptamer-functionalized SERS tags for synchronous detection of Acinetobacter baumannii and Klebsiella pneumoniae
Objective/Mechanism: A double-edged sword SERS aptasensor was developed using SPION-PEI-Au-Van nanocomposites for synchronous detection of K. pneumoniae and A. baumannii in food and clinical samples.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Shows a limit of detection was 10 cells/mL with a linear range of 50-10(5) cells/mL for both KP and AB.

Title: A SERS bioassay based on vancomycin-modified PEI-interlayered nanocomposite and aptamer-functionalized SERS tags for synchronous detection of Acinetobacter baumannii and Klebsiella pneumoniae
Objective/Mechanism: A double-edged sword SERS aptasensor was developed using SPION-PEI-Au-Van nanocomposites for synchronous detection of K. pneumoniae and A. baumannii in food and clinical samples.

Title: Aptamer-based assay for rapid detection, surveillance, and screening of pathogenic Leptospira in water samples
Objective/Mechanism: Development of an aptamer-gold nanoparticle-based colorimetric assay for pathogenic Leptospira detection.

Title: A HCR based multivalent aptamer amplifier for ultrasensitive detection of Salmonella
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a hybridization chain reaction (HCR) based multivalent aptamer (multi-Apt) as an effective signal amplifier for the sensitive detection of Salmonella.

Title: A HCR based multivalent aptamer amplifier for ultrasensitive detection of Salmonella
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a hybridization chain reaction (HCR) based multivalent aptamer (multi-Apt) as an effective signal amplifier for the sensitive detection of Salmonella.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Could detect Salmonella with multi-apt as low as 7 cfu/mL with a broad detection range of 10 to 10(7) cfu/mL.
Stability: The signals generated by the multi-Apt amplifier with different storage times at 4°C have remained unchanged over the past month.

Title: A universal bacterial sensor created by integrating a light modulating aptamer complex with photoelectrochemical signal readout
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a signal-on photoelectrochemical biosensor for detecting peptidoglycan.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Demonstrate a limit-of-detection of 82 pg/mL (13 pM) in buffer and 239 pg/mL (37 pM) in urine for peptidoglycan and 1913 CFU/mL for Escherichia coli in urine.

Title: Dual Synthetic Receptor-Based Sandwich Electrochemical Sensor for Highly Selective and Ultrasensitive Detection of Pathogenic Bacteria at the Single-Cell Level
Objective/Mechanism: An electrochemical sandwich sensor was developed for the detection of a single bacterial cell based on dual recognition by the bacteria-imprinted polymer film (BIF) and aptamer (Au@Fc-Apt).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The sensor could detect as low as 10 CFU/mL in a milk sample and 1 CFU/mL in PBS with a linear range from 10 to 10(5) CFU/mL for S. aureus.
Stability: After storage at 4°C for 17 days, the sensor still retained about 92% of the initial detection signal.

Title: Rolling Circle Amplification/G-Quadruplex-Based Dual-Signal Ratiometric Electrochemical Aptasensor for Ultrasensitive Detection of Pathogenic Bacteria
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a ratiometric dual-signal electrochemical biosensor for ultrasensitive detection of S. aureus based on an aptamer recognition-induced rolling circle amplification (RCA)/G-quadruplex strategy.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Showed a good linear relationship between 10–10(6) CFU/mL with a detection limit of 10 CFU/mL.

Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers against B. cereus across different growth phases and develop an impedance-based aptasensor immobilized on a GCE/Au surface for its detection.

Title: Development of a label-free impedimetric aptasensor for the detection of Acinetobacter baumannii bacteria
Objective/Mechanism: An electrochemical aptasensor was developed using an aptamer immobilized on the surface of a CSPE modified with the nanocomposite Fe3O4@SiO2@Glyoxal (Gly) for A. baumannii detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Specifically detect A. baumannii in the concentration range from 1.0 × 10(3)–1.0 × 10(8) CFU/mL and with a detection limit of 150 CFU/mL.
Stability: The current response from 0 day to 28 days was 94.3%, 90%, and 86.5% of the primary Rct response of the aptasensor remained at 4°C after 14, 21 and 28 days, respectively.

Title: Specific Instantaneous Detection of Klebsiella pneumoniae for UTI Diagnosis with a Plasmonic Gold Nanoparticle Conjugated Aptasensor
Objective/Mechanism: Developed localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) aptasensor using a tailor-made plasmonic aptamer-gold nanoparticle (AuNP) for detection of Klebsiella pneumoniae.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: LoD as low as 3.4 × 10(3) CFU/mL within 5 min.

Title: A Novel Method for Sensitive Detection of Vibrio alginolyticus Based on Aptamer and Hybridization Chain Reaction in Aquaculture
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a method using an HCR-based multivalent aptamer (multi-Apt) for the detection of Vibrio alginolyticus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Obtained a linear range from 10 to 10(7) CFU/mL, and the limit of detection (LOD) is 3 CFU/mL.

Title: A Colorimetric/Fluorescent Dual-Mode Aptasensor for Salmonella Based on the Magnetic Separation of Aptamers and a DNA-Nanotriangle Programmed Multivalent Aptamer
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a colorimetric/fluorescent dual-mode method based on a DNA-nanotriangle programmed multivalent aptamer (NTri-Multi-Apt) for the detection of Salmonella.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a linear range of 1.0 × 10(2)–1.0 × 10(7) CFU/mL and LODs of 316 and 60 CFU/mL for colorimetric and fluorescent detection, respectively.

Title: A Colorimetric/Fluorescent Dual-Mode Aptasensor for Salmonella Based on the Magnetic Separation of Aptamers and a DNA-Nanotriangle Programmed Multivalent Aptamer

Objective/Mechanism: Developed a nanoprobe (DTAAT) based on DNA tetrahedral supported hybridization chain reaction (HCR) for in situ analysis of SA.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Detect SA with the detection limit as low as 26 CFU/mL and linear range of 50-5×10(6) CFU/mL.

Title: Sandwich-Type Electrochemical Aptasensor for Highly Sensitive and Selective Detection of Pseudomonas Aeruginosa Bacteria Using a Dual Signal Amplification Strategy
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a sandwich-type electrochemical aptasensor using a carbon screen-printed electrode (MIL101(Cr)/MWCNT) and AgNPs/C-g-C3N4/Apt for P. aeruginosa detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a limit of detection of 1 CFU/mL and a linear range of 10 to 10(7) CFU/mL.
Stability: The DPV current intensity of the aptasensor for 10(5) CFU/mL of P. aeruginosa was approximately 92.4% of its initial signals after 21 days stored at 4°C.

Objective/Mechanism: An ultrasensitive multicolour electrochromic platform based on a closed bipolar electrode (BPE) was developed for visual sensing of P. aeruginosa.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The detection limit was as low as 0.33 CFU/mL, and the linear range was 10(0)-10(8) CFU/mL within 30 min by the naked eye.

Title: A SERS biosensor based on aptamer-based Fe3O4@SiO2@Ag magnetic recognition and embedded SERS probes for ultrasensitive simultaneous detection of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a SERS biosensor based on aptamer-modified Fe3O4@SiO2@Ag and Au-MPBA/DTNB@Ag for simultaneous detection of S.aureus and E.coli.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Rapidly detect S. aureus with the limit of detection (LOD) of 1 CFU/mL in 20 min and a linear range from 10(1) ∼ 10(8) CFU/mL.

Title: An electrochemical and colorimetric dual-mode aptasensor for Staphylococcus aureus based on a multifunctional MOF and magnetic separation technique
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a colorimetric and electrochemical dual-mode aptasensor based on ssDNA-Au/CuMOF and MB-Apt for S. aureus detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display a broad linear range from 10 to 10(8) CFU/mL, with colorimetric minimum resolution of 48 CFU/mL, and electrochemical detection limit of 5 CFU/mL.

Title: Joint concanavalin A-aptamer enabled dual recognition for anti-interference visual detection of Salmonella typhimurium in complex food matrices
Objective/Mechanism: A dual recognition platform based on Concanavalin A (Con A)-aptamer joint strategy for sensitive determination of S. typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited linear range of 7.0 × 10(1) ∼ 7.0 × 10(9) CFU/mL, along with a detection limit as low as 23 CFU/mL.

Title: A signal-off aptasensor for the determination of Acinetobacter baumannii by using methylene blue as an electrochemical probe
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an electrochemical aptasensor with Apt/MWCNT@Fe3O4@SiO2-Cl/CSPE nanocomposite to detect A. baumannii.

Title: Assessment of the growth inhibition and anti-biofilm activity of aptamer (PmA2G02) against Proteus mirabilis 1429T
Objective/Mechanism: Inhibit biofilm formation, adhesion, and mobility, along with a reduction in biofilm-related genes, namely rsbA, fliC2 & fimD, in P. mirabilis.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Aptamer treatment resulted in a 50% reduction in biofilm thickness and a 2.29-fold and 1.34-fold decrease in mRNA expression of the fliC2 and fimD genes, respectively.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): Aptamer treatment did not significantly affect cell viability.

Title: Rapid Detection and Identification of Vancomycin-Sensitive Bacteria Using an Electrochemical Apta-Sensor
Objective/Mechanism: A portable electrochemical biosensor was developed for the identification of Gram-positive bacteria based on a vancomycin-modified screen-printed carbon electrode.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Demonstrated that capture was achieved in 10 min, with a limit of detection of only 2.7 CFU/mL.

Title: Rapid Detection and Identification of Vancomycin-Sensitive Bacteria Using an Electrochemical Apta-Sensor
Objective/Mechanism: A portable electrochemical biosensor was developed for the identification of Gram-positive bacteria based on a vancomycin-modified screen-printed carbon electrode.

Title: Cell-SELEX for aptamer discovery and its utilization in constructing electrochemical biosensor for rapid and highly sensitive detection of Legionella pneumophila serogroup 1
Objective/Mechanism: Identify an aptamer against L. pneumophila SG1 and develop an electrochemical aptasensor for its detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Limit of Detection (LOD): 4.6 CFU/mL and linear trend ranging from 10 to 10(8) CFU/mL.

Title: Next-Generation Wound Care: Aptamer-Conjugated Polydiacetylene/Polyurethane Nanofibrous Biosensors for Selective In Situ Colorimetric Detection of Pseudomonas
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer-modified polydiacetylene-based electrospun nanofibrous wound dressing for the detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The LOD for the aptamer-modified membrane P-F23 was 1.42 × 10(6) CFU/cm^2.

Title: Next-Generation Wound Care: Aptamer-Conjugated Polydiacetylene/Polyurethane Nanofibrous Biosensors for Selective In Situ Colorimetric Detection of Pseudomonas
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer-modified polydiacetylene-based electrospun nanofibrous wound dressing for the detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The LOD for the aptamer-modified membrane P-St21Lp17 was 4.46 × 10(6) CFU/cm^2.

Title: Sensitive and on-Site Detection of Staphylococcus aureus Based on CRISPR/Cas 13a-Assisted Chemiluminescence Resonance Energy Transfer
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a CRISPR/Cas 13a-assisted CRET-based strategy for the detection of S. aureus in real samples.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Successfully detected S. aureus in drinking water and milk with detection limits of 20 and 30 cfu/mL, respectively, within the recovery of 90.07–105.50%.

Title: Competitive Electrochemical Apta-Assay Based on cDNA-Ferrocene and MXenes for Staphylococcus aureus Surface Protein A Detection
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a competitive aptasensor based on a ferrocene (Fc)-labeled cDNA hybridized (cDNA-Fc S13) on a specific aptamer (APT) for PrA in the presence of MXene nanosheets for the indirect detection of S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Displayed a linear range of 10–125 nM, an LOD of 3.33 nM, and a response time under 40 min.

Title: Rapid detection of Brucella cells using a gold nanoparticle-based aptasensor via a simple colorimetric method
Target Organism: Brucella Melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine and Brucella Abortus strain RB51 vaccine
Objective/Mechanism: Detection of Brucella cells using a biosensor, based on gold nanoparticles (GNPs) and a specific aptamer, via a colorimetric reaction.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Able to detect 1.5 × 10(1) CFU/mL with a linear range of 1.5 × 10(1)-1.5 × 10(8) CFU/mL of the bacterial cells.

Title: Visual fluorescence detection of Listeria monocytogenes with CRISPR-Cas12a aptasensor
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptasensor utilizing carboxylated magnetic beads and Cas12a to detect L. monocytogenes.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Demonstrates excellent sensitivity towards L. monocytogenes, with a lowest detection limit (LOD) of 57.15 CFU/mL and a linear range of 4×10(2) to 4×10(7) CFU/mL.

Title: Colourimetric and SERS dual-mode aptasensor using Au@Ag and magnetic nanoparticles for the detection of Campylobacter jejuni
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a dual-mode aptasensor using aptamer-conjugated Au@Ag NPs for the effective detection of C. jejuni.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibit a wider linear range (1.8 × 10(1)–10(8) CFU/mL and a lower limit of detection of 6 CFU/mL.

Title: Electrocatalytic aptasensor for bacterial detection exploiting ferricyanide reduction by methylene blue on mixed PEG/aptamer monolayers
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a disposable electrocatalytic “off–on” sensor for E. coli on Au SPE.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a linear range of 10 to 1000 CFU/mL and LOD of 10 CFU/mL E. coli in 30 min.

Title: "Five birds one stone" tri-modal monitoring driven lab-on-magnetic aptasensor for accurate pathogen detection and enhanced germicidal application
Objective/Mechanism: A fluorescence-colorimetric-photothermal tri-modal sensing platform was developed for the detection of S. aureus by apt/KCl@CDs and magnetic multi-walled carbon nanotube composites (M-MWCNTs).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The detection limits of fluorescence, colorimetric and photothermal models were 4.81 cfu/mL, 3.40 cfu/mL and 6.74 cfu/mL, respectively with the same linear range of 10 - 1.0 ×10(7) cfu/mL.

Title: One-pot rapid visual detection of E. coli O157:H7 by label-free AuNP-based plasmonic-aptasensor in water sample
Objective/Mechanism: A label-free biosensor was developed using an aptamer and single-pot Au nanoparticle (AuNP) for the detection of E. coli O157:H7.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Could identify target bacteria with as few as 250 CFU/ml in 15 min or less.
Stability: After five days (stored at 4°C) from synthesizing PG-apt-AuNPs, its performance in detecting 10(5) CFU/ml of E. coli O157:H7 is similar to that of newly synthesized biosensor.

Title: Aptamer-mediated double strand displacement amplification with microchip electrophoresis for ultrasensitive detection of Salmonella typhimurium
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer-mediated double SDA-MCE method for ultrasensitive detection of S. typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a linear range of 30–1.0 × 10(5) CFU/mL and the limit of detection for S. typhimurium down to 6 CFU/mL.

Title: DNA origami-enhanced binding of aptamers to Staphylococcus aureus cells
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a DNA origami-based biosensor for the detection of SA.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Five-times higher affinity of the aptamer-functionalized DNA origami compared to pure aptamers.

Title: Label-free electrochemical aptasensor for detection of Acinetobacter baumannii: Unveiling the kinetic behavior of reduced graphene oxide v/s graphene oxide
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an electrochemical aptasensor that employed a screen-printed carbon electrode modified with both graphene oxide (GO) and reduced graphene oxide (rGO) for the detection of AB.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved an impressive limit of detection of 10 CFU/mL and a linear range of 10 to 10(9) CFU/mL.
Stability: The current response of aptasensor exhibited negligible changes in the CV signal even after the 4-week storage period.

Title: Development of an electrochemical sensitive aptasensor based on a zeolite imidazolate framework-8 and gold nanoparticles for the determination of Staphylococcus aureus bacteria
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an electrochemical aptasensor based on a glassy carbon electrode (GCE) modified with zeolite imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF 8) and gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) for the detection of S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Showed a linear response in the concentration range of 1.5 × 10(1) to 1.5 × 10(7) CFU mL−1 and a detection limit of 3.4 CFU/mL.
Stability: Response of the proposed aptasensor reached 98.9%, 94.3%, and 92.8% of the initial response on the first, second, and third days, respectively, when kept at 4°C.

Title: A novel paper-based electrochemiluminescence biosensor for non-destructive detection of pathogenic bacteria in real samples
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a paper-based electrochemiluminescence (ECL) aptasensor based on a Ru-MOF-5 NFs modified Indium tin oxide (ITO) electrode for the detection of S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a linear range from 5 to 10(8) CFU/mL, and a limit of detection (LOD) of 1 CFU/mL.
Stability: After 9 days at 4°C, the ECL signal of aptsensor retained 95.8% of its initial value, suggesting satisfactory storage stability.

Title: Colorimetric and fluorescent dual-mode detection of Escherichia coli using Fe3O4 nanoparticle coated with fluorescein-labeled aptamer
Target: Outer membrane protein Ag1 (E. coli OMP Ag1)
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a dual-mode colorimetric and fluorescence assay employing Fe3O4 nanoparticles (NPs) coated with FAM-Apt for the identification of E. coli.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Acheived an impressive limit of detection (LOD) of 10 CFU/mL in the colorimetric mode and 6 CFU/mL in the fluorescence mode.

Title: Colorimetric aptasensor for Listeria monocytogenes detection using dual functional Fe3O4@MIL-100(Fe) with magnetic separation and oxidase-like activities in food samples
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a colorimetric aptasensor based on magnetic responsiveness and oxidase-like activity of Fe3O4@MIL-100(Fe) for the detection of L.monocytogenes.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The linear range was from 10(2) to 10(7) CFU/mL, with the limit of detection as low as 14 CFU/mL.

Title: Aptamer-functionalized Fe3O4/MWCNTs@Mo-CDs nanozyme for rapid colorimetric detection toward Escherichia coli
Objective/Mechanism: Peroxidase (POD)-like Fe3O4/MWCNTs@Mo-CDs (FMMC) nanozyme was developed for the colorimetric detection of E. coli.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Had a wide linear range of 10(1)–10(6) CFU/mL, low LOD of 0.978 CFU/mL.

Objective/Mechanism: Developed a bi-module biosensor using FsC-MNPs and aptamer-CDs to discriminate Campylobacter and Aliarcobacter.
Method: Whole Cell-SELEX with the High-Throughput Sequencing (HTS)

Objective/Mechanism: Developed a fluorescence and colorimetry dual-mode sensor to detect S. aureus by MnO2 NSs and CDs.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Had a broad linear range of 37 ∼ 3.7 × 10(6) CFU/mL and low detection limits of 9 CFU/mL (ratiometric fluorescence) and 22 CFU/mL (colorimetry).

Title: Ultra-sensitive and rapid detection of Salmonella enterica and Staphylococcus aureus to single-cell level by aptamer-functionalized carbon nanotube field-effect transistor biosensors
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer-functionalized CNT-FET biosensor for the detection of these foodborne pathogens.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Could detect S. enterica at a limit of detection (LOD) as low as 1 CFU in PBS buffer with a linear range from 62.5–6.4 × 10(4) CFU/mL.

Title: Ultra-sensitive and rapid detection of Salmonella enterica and Staphylococcus aureus to single-cell level by aptamer-functionalized carbon nanotube field-effect transistor biosensors
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer-functionalized CNT-FET biosensor for the detection of these foodborne pathogens.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Could detect S. aureus at a limit of detection (LOD) as low as 1.2 CFU in PBS buffer with a linear range from 10(2)-1.28 × 10(4) CFU/mL.

Title: Plasma-based ultrasensitive detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis ESAT6/CFP10 fusion antigen using a CRISPR-driven aptamer fluorescence testing (CRAFT)
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a CRAFT (CRISPR-Driven Aptamer Fluorescence Testing) assay designed for the rapid and sensitive detection of M.tb. antigens from peripheral blood.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a detection limit of 0.1 ag/mL EC proteins (equivalent to 3 protein particles per mL) within 120 min from the plasma sample.

Title: Bioimaging with fluorescent nucleic-acid aptamers for the specific detection and quantification of Pseudomonas aeruginosa alone and in heterogeneous bacterial populations
Objective/Mechanism: Develop a fluorescent aptamer for detecting Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: 73.79% of live P. aeruginosa cells (3102/4204) were labeled by the Cy5‐F23 aptamer, compared to only 0.06% of live S. aureus (4/6767).
Stability: The aptamer remains highly stable for 72 hours.

Title: Screening and characterization of nucleic acid aptamers targeting Brucella surface antigens: identification and analysis of their corresponding binding sites
Target: Outer membrane protein BamA (β-barrel assembly machinery A)
Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers against Brucella and conjugate them to liposomes for selective recognition and significantly reduced bacterial invasion of host cells.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: WS-6 significantly reduced Brucella invasion, as evidenced by a decrease in qPCR Ct from 22.34 to 20.64 (P < 0.05), confirming a reduced intracellular bacterial load.
Stability: The aptamer demonstrated stable binding to the Brucella S2 vaccine across a temperature range of 16–50°C, with optimal binding observed between 16°C and 50°C and under neutral conditions (pH 7.6) in 2h.

Title: Screening and characterization of nucleic acid aptamers targeting Brucella surface antigens: identification and analysis of their corresponding binding sites
Objective/Mechanism: Binds BamA β-barrel assembly protein → blocks/inhibits bacterial invasion into host cells.

Title: Introduce a novel, extremely sensitive aptamer against staphylococcal enterotoxin type D
Objective/Mechanism: Isolate high-affinity ssDNA aptamers with specificity for SED.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The limit of detection (LOD) for SED was determined to be 45 nM.
Determination of affinity method: Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) and Enzyme-Linked Apta-Sorbent Assay (ELASA)

Title: Aptamer-functionalized graphene quantum dots combined with artificial intelligence detect bacteria for urinary tract infections
Objective/Mechanism: Develop an aptamer-functionalized graphene quantum dots integrated with an artificial intelligence detection system (AG-AI detection system) for the detection of E. coli.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibits a wide linearity (10(3)-10(9) CFU/mL) and a low detection limit (3.38×10(2) CFU/mL).

Title: Inhibition of Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli adhesion via aptamers prevents infection in IPEC-J2 cells
Objective/Mechanism: An aptamer was identified to effectively inhibit the adhesion of ETEC K88 to intestinal epithelial cell IPEC-J2 and reduce ETEC K88-induced cytotoxicity in IPEC-J2 cells in vitro.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: K88-Apt A04 may more effectively displace ETEC K88 and induce less cytotoxicity than K88-Apt 37, as it resulted in lower TNF-α expression.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): K88-Apt A04 indicated the lowest cytotoxicity (5.18%) at 100 nM

Title: Inhibition of Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli adhesion via aptamers prevents infection in IPEC-J2 cells
Objective/Mechanism: An aptamer was identified to effectively inhibit the adhesion of ETEC K88 to intestinal epithelial cell IPEC-J2 and reduce ETEC K88-induced cytotoxicity in IPEC-J2 cells in vitro.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: K88-Apt A04 may more effectively displace ETEC K88 and induce less cytotoxicity than K88-Apt 37, as it resulted in lower TNF-α expression.
Cytotoxicity (cell viability): K88-Apt 37 revealed the lowest cytotoxicity (8.77%) at 50 nM.

Title: Simultaneous and sensitive detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and SARS-CoV-2 antigens employing an electrochemical impedance spectroscopy aptasensor
Objective/Mechanism: Develop an EIS-based aptasensor fabricated to detect MPT64 and S-glycoprotein simultaneously, employing a dual-platform approach on a screen-printed gold electrode (SPGE).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved detection limits of 0.053 pg/mL in buffer and in human serum of 0.085 pg/mL with a linear range of 0.01 pg/mL to 10 pg/mL in both buffer and human serum.
Stability: The aptasensor maintained good storage stability for up to 22 days.

Title: Aptamer-molecularly imprinted polymer sensors for the detection of bacteria in water
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an electrochemical sensor based on aptamer-molecularly imprinted polymer (Apta-MIP) for the multiplexed detection of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Can detect E. coli with a limit of detection of 2 CFU/mL and exhibited a broad dynamic range from 1 CFU/mL to 10(8) CFU/mL.

Title: Aptamer-molecularly imprinted polymer sensors for the detection of bacteria in water
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an electrochemical sensor based on aptamer-molecularly imprinted polymer (Apta-MIP) for the multiplexed detection of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Can detect S. aureus with a limit of detection of 4 CFU/mL and exhibited a broad dynamic range from 1 CFU/mL to 10(8) CFU/mL.
