Title: Self-reduced Pd nanoparticles on NiMn-LDHs with superior catalytic activity for signal amplification in electrochemical aptasensing of Mycobacterium tuberculosis ESAT-6 antigen
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an electrochemical aptasensor using NiMn-layered double hydroxides@palladium nanoparticles (NiMn-LDHs@PdNPs) for detecting the ESAT-6 antigen in human serum.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The aptasensor exhibited a wide linear detection range of 75 pg/mL to 10 ng/mL with a low limit of detection (LOD) of 0.629 pg/mL.
Stability: Aptasensor was stored at 4°C for and after 30 days, the current remained approximately 80% of the initial value.

Title: Ultrasensitive electrochemical aptasensor for Pseudomonas aeruginosa detection using N-doped MWCNTs/AgNPs nanocomposite
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an electrochemical P.A. biosensor based on N-MWCNTs/AgNPs-10/Apt for the detection of P. aeruginosa.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a wide linear detection range from 10(-1) to 10(6) CFU/mL, and the limit of detection is 0.0798 CFU/mL.

Title: Portable AI-driven electrochemical aptasensor for real-time Staphylococcus aureus detection in food and beverages
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a portable electrochemical aptasensor integrated with machine learning using SPCE/AuNPs for the detection of S. aureus in food and beverage samples.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The lowest detection limit for S. aureus was 1 CFU/mL.

Title: Smartphone-Based Fluorescence/Colorimetric Dual-Mode Aptasensor for the Detection of Salmonella Using Multivalent Aptamer and CHA Amplification
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a dual-mode portable fluorescent/colorimetric aptasensor, leveraging multivalent aptamer competitive assays and catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) for the detection of Salmonella.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Enables the quantitative detection of Salmonella within a linear range of 10 to 10(7) CFU/mL, with detection limits of 28 CFU/mL for colorimetric detection and 10 CFU/mL for fluorescent detection.

Title: Real-Time and Selective Detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in Beef Samples Using a g-C3N4-Doped Multimetallic Perovskite-Based Electrochemical Aptasensor
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an electrochemical aptasensor based on aptamer functionalized FeCoCuNiO-g-C3N4 nanocomposite for the detection of P. aeruginosa in food samples.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a low detection limit of 3.03 CFU/mL and over a range of 1 × 10(1)–1 × 10(7) CFU/mL.

Title: Ultrasensitive Aptamer-Based Metal-Organic Framework-on-Metal-Organic Framework Platform for Clinical Detection of KPC-2 Klebsiella pneumoniae and Multidrug-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii
Target Organism: Klebsiella Pneumoniae carbapenemase 2-expressing K. Pneumoniae (KPC-2 KP)
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a dual nanozyme-powered colorimetric aptasensor leveraging a cascade amplification mechanism, a metal-organic framework (MOF)-on-MOF nanostructure with peroxidase-like activity for detection of KPC-2 K. pneumoniae and MDR-AB.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The system achieves selective bacterial capture within 40 min, quantifying 10–10(8) CFU/mL with a detection limit of 7 CFU/mL for KPC-2 KP.

Title: Ultrasensitive Aptamer-Based Metal-Organic Framework-on-Metal-Organic Framework Platform for Clinical Detection of KPC-2 Klebsiella pneumoniae and Multidrug-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a dual nanozyme-powered colorimetric aptasensor leveraging a cascade amplification mechanism, a metal-organic framework (MOF)-on-MOF nanostructure with peroxidase-like activity for detection of KPC-2 K. pneumoniae and MDR-AB.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The system achieves selective bacterial capture within 40 min, quantifying 10–10(8) CFU/mL with a detection limit of 6 CFU/mL for MDR-AB.

Title: A novel fluorescent aptasensor using magnetic silica nanospheres and Ag@MOF nanocomposites for extraction and detection of Salmonella Typhimurium in eggs
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a fluorescent platform based on an aptamer-Ag@MOF and Fe3O4@KCC‐1 probes for the detection of S. Typhimurium in eggs.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Achieved a linear detection range of 7.5 to 7.5 × 10⁶ CFU/mL, a detection limit of 4.61 CFU/mL, and a total detection time of 90 min.

Title: SERS-based aptasensor for culture-free detection of Escherichia coli in urinary tract infection diagnosis
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a SERS-based aptasensor for the detection of E. coli.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Demonstrated a detection limit of 5.9 × 10(3) CFU/mL, which is well below the UTI cutoff value.

Title: Target-triggered hybrid chain amplified fluorescence aptasensor based on label-free dye and MnO2 nanosheets system for Escherichia coli detection
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a label-free fluorescent detection system leveraging target-triggered hybridization chain reaction (HCR) amplification for E. coli detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a detection limit of 17 CFU/mL and a broad dynamic range from 5.0 × 10(1) ~ 5.0 × 10(7) CFU/mL.

Title: 3D DNA walkers integrated with self-reporting MOFs: Pioneering ratiometric electrochemical sensing for Staphylococcus aureus
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a ratiometric electrochemical aptasensor utilizing a magnetic 3D DNA walking machine and self-assembly of MOF for the sensitive detection of S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Demonstrates a detection range from 10 to 2 × 10(5) CFU/mL and achieves a low LOD of 2.3 CFU/mL.
Stability: After a duration of seven days, the ratio value maintained 91.89% of its initial intensity.

Title: A novel strategy for ultrasensitive detection and effective inactivation of Staphylococcus aureus based on Fe3O4-QCS-PEI-Cu-aptamer and ladder-branch HCR
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an integrated strategy based on Fe3O4-quaternary ammonium chitosan-polyetherimide-Cu-aptamer (Fe3O4-QCS-PEI-Cu-aptamer) and ladder-branch hybridization chain reaction (HCR) for the detection and inactivation of S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The sensor demonstrated a limit of detection (LOD) of 3 CFU/mL for S. aureus and, under near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, achieved an antimicrobial efficiency of 99.946%.

Title: Cascaded Strand Displacement Amplification and CRISPR/Cas12a Aptasensor Utilizing MoS2 Nanoflowers for Colorectal Cancer Biomarker Porphyromonas gingivalis Detection
Objective/Mechanism: Identify specific aptamers targeting P. gingivalis and develop an aptasensor based on MoS2 nanoflowers that integrates strand displacement amplification and CRISPR/Cas12a double-amplification for detection.

Title: Fluorescent aptasensor for detection of Salmonella typhimurium using boric acid-functionalized terbium metal-organic framework and magnetic nanoparticles
Objective/Mechanism: A fluorescent detection platform was developed using boric acid-functionalized terbium metal–organic framework (BA-Tb-MOF) and carboxyl-modified magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) to identify S. typhimurium.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Showed an inverse linear relationship within the range of 10(1)–10(9) CFU/mL, and the detection limit was 4 CFU/mL.

Title: Au@Fe3O4 Nanoparticle-Based Colorimetric Aptasensor for Noninvasive Screening of Colorectal Cancer via Detection of Parvimonas micra
Objective/Mechanism: Isolate aptamers against P. micra and develop colorimetric aptsensor using Au@Fe3O4 nanoparticles.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Demonstrated a linear response across a range of 10–10(8) CFU/mL for P. micra with a limit of detection of 11 CFU/mL.

Title: Au@Fe3O4 Nanoparticle-Based Colorimetric Aptasensor for Noninvasive Screening of Colorectal Cancer via Detection of Parvimonas micra

Title: Nanoparticle-Enhanced Acoustic Wave Biosensor Detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in Food
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a biosensor for detecting P. aeruginosa in whole milk samples using an aptamer functionalized antifouling linking molecule 3-(2-mercaptoethanoxy)propanoic acid (HS-MEG-COOH), and another one with the addition of AuNPs.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a linear range 10(2)-10(5) CFU/mL and limit of detection (LOD) of 86 CFU/mL in PBS and 157 CFU/mL in milk, and with AuNPs, reducing the extrapolated LOD to 68 CFU/mL in PBS and 46 CFU/mL in milk.

Title: Laser-induced graphene-based aptasensor for the selective detection of Escherichia coli in urine samples
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an impedance biosensor using a Laser-Induced Graphene-based (LIG) electrode for the detection of E. coli in urine samples.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The aptasensor showed a linear response to E. coli over the range 10(0)-10(3) CFU/mL and LOD of 9 CFU/mL in PBS.

Title: Study of Bacteriostasis of Kaempferide on Foodborne Pathogenic Bacteria by Indirect Determination of Capillary Electrophoresis
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer-based capillary sieving electrophoresis (CE)-Laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) detection of three bacteria, Vibrio parahaemolyticus, Escherichia coli, and Staphylococcus aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The measured limit of detection (LOD) for V. parahaemolyticus was 3.70 × 10(6) CFU/mL and a linear range of 0.80-124 × 10(7) CFU/mL.

Title: Study of Bacteriostasis of Kaempferide on Foodborne Pathogenic Bacteria by Indirect Determination of Capillary Electrophoresis
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer-based capillary sieving electrophoresis (CE)-Laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) detection of three bacteria, Vibrio parahaemolyticus, Escherichia coli, and Staphylococcus aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The measured limit of detection (LOD) for E. coli was 1.28 × 10(7) CFU/mL and a linear range of 6.50 - 153 × 10(7) CFU/mL.

Title: Study of Bacteriostasis of Kaempferide on Foodborne Pathogenic Bacteria by Indirect Determination of Capillary Electrophoresis

Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The measured limit of detection (LOD) for S. aureus was 1.67 × 10(7) CFU/mL and a linear range of 3.00-150 × 10(7) CFU/mL.

Title: Self-protective DNAzyme-based dual-responsive three-way Y-probe for simultaneous determination of multiple pathogenic bacteria
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a DNAzyme-based self-protecting dual-response three-way Y nanoprobe (SD-DTY) for the simultaneous detection of two foodborne pathogens.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The limit of detection was 3.2 cfu/mL, and the linear range was 10-10(5) cfu/mL, with a 2-hour response time.

Title: Self-protective DNAzyme-based dual-responsive three-way Y-probe for simultaneous determination of multiple pathogenic bacteria
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a DNAzyme-based self-protecting dual-response three-way Y nanoprobe (SD-DTY) for the simultaneous detection of two foodborne pathogens.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The limit of detection was 3.7 cfu/mL, and the linear range was 10-10(5) cfu/mL, with a 2-hour response time.

Title: Ultrasensitive electrochemical biosensor for bacteria detection based on Fe3O4@COF-AuNPs and trigging isothermal circular amplification
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an ultrasensitive electrochemical biosensor based on magnetic nanocomposite material Fe3O4@COF-AuNPs and triggering isothermal circular amplification (TICA) for E. coli detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The detection limit (LOD) was 10 CFU/mL, with a linear range of 10(2)−10(9) CFU/mL, and the detection time was 1 h.
Stability: The sensor was stored at 4°C, and the signal value decreased by only 6.28 % over 30 days.

Objective/Mechanism: Developed a SERS aptasensor based on aptamer-magnetic graphene oxide (MGO) and dual-functional Au NSs@Ag NPs probes for simultaneous detection of E. coli and S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The SERS intensity shows a good linear relationship over a range of 50 to 10(6) CFU/mL, with a detection limit of 16 CFU/mL for E. coli.

Title: SERS-based Aptasensor using Au NSs@Ag NPs/magnetic graphene oxide assemblies for simultaneous detection of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a SERS aptasensor based on aptamer-magnetic graphene oxide (MGO) and dual-functional Au NSs@Ag NPs probes for simultaneous detection of E. coli and S. aureus.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The SERS intensity shows a good linear relationship over a range of 50 to 10(6) CFU/mL, with a detection limit of 20 CFU/mL for S. aureus.

Title: Improving electrochemical aptasensor sensitivity for Bacillus cereus spore detection in food safety applications
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an electrochemical aptasensor for the detection of B. cereus spores.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: An aptasensor based on three aptamers exhibited a wide dynamic range (10(2)–10(7) CFU/mL) and a low limit of detection (∼1 CFU/mL) using only 15 μL of sample.

Title: Silver-decorated nanobeads for high-performance and flexible analysis of Shigella dysenteriae utilizing a paper-based aptasensor
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an Ag/MBs-modified paper-based aptasensor to detect S. dysenteriae.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: MB-based assays achieve broad linearity (DPV = 10(2)–10(8) CFU/mL, EIS = 10(1)–10(9) CFU/mL) and high sensitivity (DPV = 90 CFU/mL, EIS = 8.09 CFU/mL).
Stability: Long stability of up to 28 days at 4°C.

Title: In vitro selection of DNA aptamers to anthrax spores with electrochemiluminescence detection
Objective/Mechanism: Develop an aptamer–magnetic bead-electrochemiluminescence (AM-ECL) sandwich assay for detecting anthrax spores.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display broad dynamic range equivalent to 10– 6×10(6) anthrax spores.
Determination of affinity method: ECL-based and Colorimetric Peroxidase-Based Aptamer Plate Binding Assay

Title: Use of magnetic beads in selection and detection of biotoxin aptamers by electrochemiluminescence and enzymatic methods
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer-based electrochemiluminescence assay using a dsDNA aptamer for biotoxin detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Detection limit of less than 40 ng in the cholera electrochemiluminescence assay.

Title: Use of magnetic beads in selection and detection of biotoxin aptamers by electrochemiluminescence and enzymatic methods
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer-based electrochemiluminescence assay using a dsDNA aptamer for biotoxin detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Detection limit of less than 10 pg SEB with electrochemiluminescence assay.

Title: Anti-Francisella tularensis DNA aptamers detect tularemia antigen from different subspecies by Aptamer-Linked Immobilized Sorbent Assay
Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers that bind specifically to the tularemia bacterial antigen from the subspecies japonica or holarctica.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The detection limit for the aptamer cocktail is 25 ng (1.7 × 10^3/ml of bacteria).

Title: Aptamer from whole-bacterium SELEX as new therapeutic reagent against virulent Mycobacterium tuberculosis
Objective/Mechanism: Identify an aptamer that binds to and improves CD4+T cells & produces IFN-γ by blocking some membrane proteins of H37Rv, decreases the bacterial number, and prolongs the survival rate in the mouse model by inhibiting the invasion of M. tuberculosis into phagocytes and CD8+T cells.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Intracellular IFN-γ levels in CD3+CD4+ T cells increased from approximately 35% (without aptamer) to approximately 55% (with the NK2). The half-life of survival in mice was prolonged by 3 days with a single injection of NK2 aptamer treatment.

Title: Development and characterization of monoclonal antibodies and aptamers against major antigens of Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis
Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers that were screened against the MAP0105c gene product.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Bound specifically to the N-terminal half of MAP0105c, and nearly all mycobacteria tested.

Title: Plastic-adherent DNA aptamer-magnetic bead and quantum dot sandwich assay for Campylobacter detection
Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers against surface proteins from C. jejuni and develop a sandwich assay ( (C2 aptamer-MB-bacteria-C3 aptamer-QD complexes) for its detection.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibits detection limits as low as an average of 2.5 cfu equivalents in buffer and 10–250 cfu in various food matrices.

Title: Selection and characterization of DNA aptamers with binding selectivity to Campylobacter jejuni using whole-cell SELEX
Target: Whole cell (bind via proteinaceous nature for cell surface target)
Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers against C. jejuni and detect them in a mixed cell population.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: ONS-23 showed high binding affinity (25–36%) for all other C. jejuni strains screened (inclusivity) and low apparent binding affinity (1–5%) with non-C. jejuni strains (exclusivity).

Title: Selection and application of ssDNA aptamers to detect active TB from sputum samples

Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers against the CFP-10.ESAT-6 heterodimer and active TB from human sputum samples.

Objective/Mechanism: Inhibits the H37Rv invasion of macrophages in vitro and activates the infection of macrophages.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Significantly decreased macrophage invasion from 64.58% (without aptamers) to 33.02% (with 10th aptamer pool), and 26.01% (with NK2).

Title: DNA aptamers as a novel approach to neutralize Staphylococcus aureus α-toxin
Objective/Mechanism: Identify aptamers that bind to and inhibit the cytotoxic activity of a-toxin and the upregulation of inflammatory cytokines TNF-a and IL-17.

Objective/Mechanism: Developed an aptamer-MB and aptamer-QD sandwich assay for the detection of C.jejuni.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Establishes a LOD between 5 and 10 C. jejuni cells/mL in sterile buffer (PBS) and chicken rinsate.

Title: A bimodal (SERS and colorimetric) aptasensor for the detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Objective/Mechanism: The dual-mode aptasensor based on SERS and colorimetry assay for the determination of P. aeruginosa.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: LOD of the aptasensor was 20 cfu/mL for SERS mode and 50 cfu·mL−1 for color mode with a linear range from 10^2 cfu/mL to 10^6 cfu/mL.

Title: Aptamer functionalized MoS2-rGO nanocomposite based biosensor for the detection of Vi antigen
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a novel aptamer functionalized MoS2-rGO-based electrochemical aptasensor for Vi polysaccharide antigen-mediated detection of enteric fever.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Responded linearly in the range between 0.1 ng/mL to 1000 ng/mL with a detection limit of 100 pg/mL.

Title: Target-induced aptamer displacement on gold nanoparticles and rolling circle amplification for ultrasensitive live Salmonella typhimurium electrochemical biosensing
Objective/Mechanism: Develop an aptasensor for ultrasensitive detection of live S. typhimurium by combining target-induced aptamer displacement on gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) deposited electrode with rolling circle amplification (RCA).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Showed a LOD of 16 CFU/mL with a wide linear detection range of 20 to 2 × 10(8) CFU/mL.
Stability: When the sensor was stored at 4°C for 10 days, the electrical signal response was 90% of that obtained at the time of preparation.

Title: An aptasensor for the detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis secreted immunogenic protein MPT64 in clinical samples towards tuberculosis detection
Objective/Mechanism: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) aptasenosor based on an IDE for the detection of MPT64.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Display LOD of 4.1 fM and the specificity and sensitivity for the sputum sample analysis 100% and 76.47%, respectively, and for the serum sample analysis 100% and 88.24%, respectively.

Title: Photo-responsive functional gold nanocapsules for inactivation of community-acquired, highly virulent, multidrug-resistant MRSA
Objective/Mechanism: Aptamers functionalization of Cur@mPEG-SH@GNRs for PTT and ROS.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Blocked biofilm formation and killed all of the trapped bacteria in 30 min during NIR stimulation.

Title: Aptasensor for the detection of Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus on contaminated surfaces
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a colorimetric aptasensor for the detection of MRSA on contaminated surfaces.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The visual detection limit was less than 100 CFU/ml and, theoretically, 2 CFU/ml, while the linear range of quantitation was 10(2)–10(5) CFU/ml.

Title: Aptamer-superparamagnetic nanoparticles capture coupling siderophore-Fe3+ scavenging actuated with carbon dots to confer an "off-on" mechanism for the ultrasensitive detection of Helicobacter pylori
Objective/Mechanism: Aptamer-modified superparamagnetic nanoparticles (SPMNPs) are used to develop a triple-module biosensor to capture H. pylori.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Exhibited a wide detection range of 10-10(7) CFU/mL and a limit of detection (LOD) as low as 1 CFU/mL.

Title: Aptamer-superparamagnetic nanoparticles capture coupling siderophore-Fe3+ scavenging actuated with carbon dots to confer an "off-on" mechanism for the ultrasensitive detection of Helicobacter pylori
Objective/Mechanism: Aptamer-modified superparamagnetic nanoparticles (SPMNPs) capture H. pylori.

Objective/Mechanism: Aptamer-modified superparamagnetic nanoparticles (SPMNPs) capture H. pylori.

Objective/Mechanism: Aptamer-modified superparamagnetic nanoparticles (SPMNPs) capture H. pylori.

Title: Single-stranded DNA aptamer-based rolling circle amplification as anti-chicken Salmonella bacteriostatic
Target Organism: Salmonella Typhimurium (S. Typhimurium) and Salmonella Enteritidis (S. Enteritidis)
Objective/Mechanism: Identify an aptamer targeting Salmonella in the form of RCA-p that could inhibit bacterial growth, multiplication, and viability.

Title: Sensitive detection of Escherichia coli in diverse foodstuffs by electrochemical aptasensor based on 2D porphyrin-based COF
Objective/Mechanism: Developed an electrochemical aptasensor using two-dimensional porphyrin-based covalent organic framework (Tph-TDC-COF) for the detection of E.coli.
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: Demonstrated an extremely low detection limit of 0.17 CFU/mL for E.coli detection within a linear range of 10 to 1 × 10(8) CFU/mL.
Stability: The aptasensor recovered to 104.3% after 15 days of storage at 4°C in 0.01 M phosphate buffer, indicating excellent stability.

Title: Aptamer-carbon quantum dots and silver nanoparticles construct a FRET sensor for sensitive detection of E. coli
Objective/Mechanism: Developed a FRET-based fluorescent biosensor by combining CQDs with Ag NPs for the rapid detection of E. coli (BL21).
Outcome/Inhibitory effect: The sensor has a linear range of 2×10(3) ∼ to 2×10(8) CFU/mL and a low detection limit of 77 CFU/mL for E. coli.
